bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第266卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 266
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 266

sentences.zh: 【後梁紀一】起強圉單閼，盡著雍執徐七月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Liang Annals 1] From the cyclical year Qiangsi-Danchi through the seventh month of Zhuoyong-Zhixu, altogether somewhat more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Liang Annals, Part 1] The record runs from the year Qiangsi-Danchi through the seventh month of Zhuoyong-Zhixu—a span of just over one year.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，梁王休兵於貝州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day Xinsi, the Prince of Liang rested his troops at Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, on the day Xinsi, the Prince of Liang gave his army a rest at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使兼侍中、東面諸道行營都統弘農郡王楊渥既得江西，驕侈益甚，謂節度判官周隱曰：「君賣人國家，何面復相見！」

translations.literal: The Huainan military governor, concurrently Palace Attendant and supreme commander of the eastern circuits, Prince of Hongnong Yang Wo, having already taken Jiangxi, became ever more arrogant and extravagant. He said to his military judge Zhou Yin: "You sold out another man's state—how dare you show your face before me again!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo, military governor of Huainan, who also held the titles of Palace Attendant and supreme commander of the eastern circuits and was Prince of Hongnong, had recently secured Jiangxi and grew still more arrogant and dissolute. He said to his military judge Zhou Yin, "You sold out someone else's kingdom—how can you bear to face me again?"

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: He then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: With that he had him executed.

sentences.zh: 由是將佐皆不自安。

translations.literal: From this the generals and aides all felt insecure.
translations.idiomatic: After this, none of his commanders and staff felt safe in their posts.

sentences.zh: 黑雲都指揮使呂師周與副指揮使綦章將兵屯上高，師周與湖南戰，屢有功，渥忌之。

translations.literal: The Black Cloud Corps commander Lü Shizhou and his deputy commander Qi Zhang led troops stationed at Shanggao. Shizhou fought repeatedly with Hunan and won many victories, and Wo grew jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shizhou, commander of the Black Cloud Corps, and his deputy Qi Zhang were encamped at Shanggao. Shizhou fought Hunan several times with repeated success, which made Wo envious.

sentences.zh: 師周懼，謀於綦章曰：「馬公寬厚，吾欲逃死焉，可乎？」

translations.literal: Shizhou was afraid and plotted with Zhang, saying, "Lord Ma is generous; I wish to flee there to save my life—would that be possible?"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Shizhou confided in Zhang: "Lord Ma is magnanimous. I mean to flee to Hunan to escape death—do you think I can?"

sentences.zh: 章曰：「茲事君自圖之，吾舌可斷，不敢洩！」

translations.literal: Zhang said, "You must plan this yourself; my tongue may be cut off, but I will not betray you!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang replied, "That is for you to decide. They may cut out my tongue, but I will never give you away!"

sentences.zh: 師周遂奔湖南，章縱其孥，使逸去。

translations.literal: Shizhou then fled to Hunan, and Zhang released his wife and children and let them escape.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhou then defected to Hunan. Zhang set his family free and allowed them to flee.

sentences.zh: 師周，揚州人也。

translations.literal: Shizhou was a native of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhou was from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 渥居喪，晝夜酣飲作樂，然十圍之燭以擊球，一燭費錢數萬。

translations.literal: While in mourning, Wo drank and made merry day and night, using candles ten arm-spans around for cuju; a single candle cost tens of thousands in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Even while in mourning, Wo spent his days and nights in drunken revelry, lighting polo matches with candles ten arm-spans thick—each candle costing tens of thousands of cash.

sentences.zh: 或單騎出遊，從者奔走道路，不知所之。

translations.literal: Sometimes he rode out alone; his attendants raced along the roads, not knowing where he was going.
translations.idiomatic: At times he would ride out alone, his escorts dashing along the roads with no idea of his destination.

sentences.zh: 左、右牙指揮使張顥、徐溫泣諫，渥怒曰：「汝謂我不才，何不殺我自為之！」

translations.literal: The left and right guards commanders Zhang Hao and Xu Wen remonstrated with tears. Wo angrily said, "You think me unfit—why not kill me and take my place yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao and Xu Wen, commanders of the left and right guards, pleaded with him in tears. Wo flew into a rage: "You think me incompetent—why not kill me and rule in my stead?"

sentences.zh: 二人懼。

translations.literal: The two were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 渥選壯士，號「東院馬軍」，廣署親信為將吏；

translations.literal: Wo selected stalwart soldiers, called them the "Eastern Courtyard Horse Army," and widely appointed trusted men as officers;
translations.idiomatic: Wo picked out strong soldiers, formed them into the "Eastern Courtyard Horse Army," and appointed many favorites as officers;

sentences.zh: 所署者恃勢驕橫，陵蔑勳舊。

translations.literal: those he appointed relied on their power, acted arrogantly, and looked down on the old meritocrats.
translations.idiomatic: those appointees abused their authority, swaggered over the veteran commanders, and treated the old guard with contempt.

sentences.zh: 顥、溫潛謀作亂。

translations.literal: Hao and Wen secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao and Xu Wen secretly plotted a coup.

sentences.zh: 渥父行密之世，有親軍數千，營於牙城之內，渥遷出於外，以其地為射場，顥、溫由是無所憚。

translations.literal: In the time of Wo's father Xingmi there had been several thousand personal troops quartered inside the yamen city; Wo moved them outside and used the ground as an archery range, so Hao and Wen no longer had anything to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wo's father Yang Xingmi, several thousand personal guards had been housed inside the yamen citadel. Wo relocated them and turned the site into an archery ground, which left Zhang Hao and Xu Wen free to act without restraint.

sentences.zh: 渥之鎮宣州也，命指揮使朱思勍、范思從、陳璠將親兵三千；

translations.literal: When Wo was military commissioner at Xuanzhou he had ordered the commanders Zhu Sinan, Fan Sicong, and Chen Fan to lead three thousand personal troops;
translations.idiomatic: When Wo governed Xuanzhou, he had ordered the commanders Zhu Sinan, Fan Sicong, and Chen Fan to lead three thousand personal troops;

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，召歸廣陵。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the position he summoned them back to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to power, he recalled them to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 顥、溫使三將從秦裴擊江西，因戍洪州，誣以謀叛，命別將陳祐往誅之。

translations.literal: Hao and Wen sent the three commanders with Qin Pei to attack Jiangxi, then garrisoned them at Hongzhou, slandered them as plotting rebellion, and ordered another commander Chen You to go execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao and Xu Wen sent the three commanders with Qin Pei to campaign in Jiangxi, then kept them as a garrison at Hongzhou, falsely accused them of treason, and dispatched another officer, Chen You, to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 祐間道兼行，六日至洪州，微服懷短兵徑入秦裴帳中，裴大驚，祐告之故，乃召思勍等飲酒，祐數思勍等罪，執而斬之。

translations.literal: You traveled by hidden routes at forced march and reached Hongzhou in six days. In plain clothes he carried a short weapon and went straight into Qin Pei's tent. Pei was greatly startled; You told him the reason, then summoned Sinan and the others to drink. You enumerated their crimes and seized and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: You took secret paths in a forced march and reached Hongzhou in six days. Dressed as a commoner and carrying a concealed blade, he entered Qin Pei's tent directly. Pei was stunned; You explained his mission, then called Sinan and the others to a drinking session, recited their alleged crimes, and had them seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 渥聞三將死，益忌顥、溫，欲誅之。

translations.literal: When Wo heard the three commanders were dead he grew still more suspicious of Hao and Wen and wished to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the three commanders were dead, Wo became still more wary of Zhang Hao and Xu Wen and resolved to kill them.

sentences.zh: 丙戍，渥晨視事，顥、溫帥牙兵二百，露刃直入庭中，渥曰：「爾思欲殺我邪？」

translations.literal: On the day Bingxu, in the morning Wo held court. Hao and Wen led two hundred guardsmen with bare blades straight into the courtyard. Wo said, "Do you mean to kill me?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingxu, Wo was holding morning audience when Zhang Hao and Xu Wen led two hundred guardsmen with naked swords straight into the courtyard. Wo cried, "Do you intend to kill me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰，「非敢然也，欲誅王左右亂政者耳！」

translations.literal: They answered, "We would not dare; we wish only to execute the men at your side who are ruining the government!"
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We would never dare—we mean only to kill the favorites around you who are wrecking the government!"

sentences.zh: 因數渥所親信十餘人之罪，曳下，以鐵□擊殺之，謂之「兵諫」。

translations.literal: They then listed the crimes of more than ten of Wo's intimates, dragged them down, and beat them to death with iron maces, calling it a "military remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: They then recited the offenses of more than a dozen of Wo's confidants, hauled them down, and clubbed them to death with iron maces in what they termed a "military remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 諸將不與之同者，顥、溫稍以法誅之，於是軍政悉歸二人，渥不能制。

translations.literal: Generals who did not side with them Hao and Wen gradually executed by law, and thereafter military and civil affairs all fell to the two men; Wo could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who would not join them were eliminated one by one on legal pretexts, until military and civil power belonged entirely to the two men and Wo could no longer restrain them.

sentences.zh: 初，梁王以河北諸鎮皆服，唯幽、滄未下，故大舉伐之，欲以堅諸鎮之心，既而潞州內叛，王燒營而還，威望大沮。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Liang had made the Hebei circuits submit, but You and Cang had not yet fallen, so he launched a great campaign against them, intending to steady the hearts of the circuits. Then Lu Prefecture rebelled within, the Prince burned his camps and returned, and his prestige suffered a great blow.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Liang had brought the Hebei circuits to heel; only Youzhou and Cangzhou still held out, so he mounted a major expedition to steady the other circuits. Then Lu Prefecture rebelled from within, he burned his camps and withdrew, and his prestige collapsed.

sentences.zh: 恐中外因此離心，欲速受禪以鎮之。

translations.literal: Fearing that inside and outside the realm would lose heart because of this, he wished quickly to receive the abdication to stabilize them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that court and provinces alike would lose heart over this, he wanted to accept the throne quickly to steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，王入館於魏，有疾，臥府中，魏博節度使羅紹威恐王襲之，入見王曰：「今四方稱兵為王患者，皆以翼戴唐室為名，王不如早滅唐以絕人望。」

translations.literal: On the day Dinghai the Prince entered quarters at Wei. He was ill and lay in the headquarters. The Weibo military governor Luo Shaowei, fearing the Prince would seize the region, came in to see him and said, "Now those who take up arms against Your Highness everywhere do so in the name of supporting the Tang. Your Highness would do well to destroy Tang early and cut off their hopes."
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dinghai the Prince lodged at Wei. Ill, he lay in the commandery mansion. Luo Shaowei, military governor of Weibo, fearing the Prince meant to seize his domain, came to see him and said, "All who raise armies against you do so claiming loyalty to the Tang. You would do well to end the Tang soon and destroy their pretext."

sentences.zh: 王雖不許而心德之，乃亟歸。

translations.literal: Although the Prince did not agree he was grateful in heart and hurried home.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince did not consent, yet he was inwardly obliged and hastened home.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，至大梁。

translations.literal: On the day Renyin he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renyin he arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，唐昭宣帝遣御史大夫薛貽矩至大梁勞王，貽矩請以臣禮見，王揖之升階，貽矩曰：「殿下功德在人，三靈改卜，皇帝方行舜、禹之事，臣安敢違！」

translations.literal: On the day Jiachen, the Tang Emperor Zhaoxuan sent the Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to Daliang to console the Prince. Yiju asked to see him with the rites of a subject; the Prince bowed him up the steps. Yiju said, "Your Highness's merit is in the hearts of the people; the three spirits have changed their choice. The Son of Heaven is about to perform the deeds of Shun and Yu—how could I dare refuse!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiachen, Emperor Zhaoxuan of Tang sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to Daliang to congratulate the Prince. Yiju asked to greet him with the ceremony due a subject; the Prince bowed him up the steps. Yiju said, "Your Highness's merit fills the hearts of the people; Heaven has shifted its mandate. The Son of Heaven is about to yield as Shun and Yu did—how could I presume to stand on ceremony?"

sentences.zh: 乃北面拜舞於庭。

translations.literal: He then faced north in the courtyard, bowed, and danced.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned north in the courtyard, kowtowed, and performed the ritual dance.

sentences.zh: 王側身避之。

translations.literal: The Prince turned aside to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince stepped aside to avoid receiving it.

sentences.zh: 貽矩還，言於帝曰：「元帥有受禪之意矣！」

translations.literal: When Yiju returned he said to the Emperor, "The Marshal already intends to receive the abdication!"
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yiju told the Emperor, "The Marshal is already set on taking the throne!"

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔，以二月禪位於梁，又遣宰相以書諭王；

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued an edict to abdicate to Liang in the second month, and also sent the chancellor with a letter instructing the Prince;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict to abdicate to Liang in the second month and sent the chancellor with a written summons to the Prince;

sentences.zh: 王辭。

translations.literal: the Prince declined.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince refused.

sentences.zh: 河東兵猶屯長孑，欲窺澤州。

translations.literal: The Hedong army was still encamped at Changzi, intending to watch for an opening at Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong army remained encamped at Changzi, watching for a chance against Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王命保平節度使康懷貞悉發京兆，同華之兵屯晉州以備之。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered the Baoping military governor Kang Huaizhen to mobilize all troops of Jingzhao, Tong, and Hua and station them at Jin Prefecture as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince ordered Kang Huaizhen, military governor of Baoping, to mobilize every soldier from Jingzhao, Tong, and Hua and post them at Jin Prefecture on guard.

sentences.zh: 二月，唐大臣共奏請昭宣帝遜位。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Tang ministers jointly memorialized asking Emperor Zhaoxuan to yield the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Tang ministers jointly submitted a memorial urging Emperor Zhaoxuan to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔宰相帥百官箋詣元帥府勸進，王遣使卻之。

translations.literal: On the day Renzi an edict ordered the chancellor to lead the hundred officials in a written petition to the Marshal's residence urging him to advance; the Prince sent a messenger to decline.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renzi an edict directed the chancellor to lead the bureaucracy in a formal petition to the Marshal's residence urging his accession; the Prince sent a messenger to refuse.

sentences.zh: 於是朝臣、籓鎮，乃至湖南、嶺南上箋勸進者相繼。

translations.literal: Thereupon court officials, military commissioners, and even Hunan and Lingnan sent successive petitions urging his advance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon courtiers, provincial governors, and even envoys from Hunan and Lingnan were sending one petition after another urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸未，王以亳州刺史李思安為北路行軍都統，將兵擊幽州。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day Guiwei, the Prince appointed Bozhou military governor Li Si'an supreme commander of the northern campaign and led troops to attack Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Guiwei, the Prince named Li Si'an, military governor of Bozhou, supreme commander of the northern expedition and sent him against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，唐昭宣帝詔薛貽矩再詣大梁諭禪位之意，又詔禮部尚書蘇循繼百官詣大梁。

translations.literal: On the day Gengyin, Emperor Zhaoxuan of Tang ordered Xue Yiju to go again to Daliang to announce the meaning of the abdication, and also ordered Minister of Rites Su Xun to follow the hundred officials to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengyin, Emperor Zhaoxuan ordered Xue Yiju to Daliang again to convey the terms of abdication, and ordered Minister of Rites Su Xun to accompany the full bureaucracy to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 鎮海、鎮東節度使吳王錢鏐遣其子傳鐐、傳瓘討盧佶於溫州。

translations.literal: The Zhenhai and Zhendong military governor, Prince of Wu Qian Liu, sent his sons Chuanliao and Chuanjin to attack Lu Zhe at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, Prince of Wu and military governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong, sent his sons Chuanliao and Chuanjin to attack Lu Zhe at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，唐昭宣帝降御札禪位於梁。

translations.literal: On the day Jiachen, Emperor Zhaoxuan of Tang issued an imperial letter in his own hand abdicating to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiachen, Emperor Zhaoxuan issued a personal edict in his own hand abdicating to Liang.

sentences.zh: 以攝中書令張文蔚為冊禮使，禮部尚書蘇循副之；

translations.literal: He appointed Acting Zhongshu Ling Zhang Wenwei envoy for the investiture rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhang Wenwei, acting Zhongshu Ling, chief envoy for the investiture rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;

sentences.zh: 攝侍中楊涉為押傳國寶使，翰林學士張策副之；

translations.literal: Acting Palace Attendant Yang She envoy to convey the imperial seal, with Hanlin Academician Zhang Ce as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Yang She, acting Palace Attendant, envoy to convey the imperial seal, with Hanlin Academician Zhang Ce as deputy;

sentences.zh: 御史大夫薛貽矩為押金寶使，尚書左丞趙光逢副之；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju envoy to escort the imperial treasures, with Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Zhao Guangfeng as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yiju, Censor-in-Chief, envoy to escort the regalia, with Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Zhao Guangfeng as deputy;

sentences.zh: 帥百官備法駕詣大梁。

translations.literal: leading the hundred officials with full ceremonial equipage to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: and they were to lead the full bureaucracy with the complete imperial procession to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 楊涉子直史館凝式言於涉曰：「大人為唐宰相，而國家至此，不可謂之無過。

translations.literal: Yang She's son, Director of the Historiography Office Yang Ningshi, said to She, "Father, you were a Tang chancellor, and the state has come to this—it cannot be said there was no fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yang She's son Ningshi, who headed the Historiography Office, told his father, "You served as a Tang chancellor, and the dynasty has come to this—you cannot claim you bear no blame.

sentences.zh: 況手持天子璽綬與人，雖保富貴，奈千載何！

translations.literal: Moreover, to hold the Son of Heaven's seal and ribbons and hand them to another—even if you preserve wealth and rank, what will posterity say!
translations.idiomatic: And now you are to carry the Son of Heaven's seal and investiture regalia to another man. You may keep your riches and rank, but what will history say of you?

sentences.zh: 盍辭之！」

translations.literal: Why not refuse!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not decline the mission?"

sentences.zh: 涉大駭曰：「汝滅吾族！」

translations.literal: She was greatly alarmed and said, "You will destroy our clan!"
translations.idiomatic: She was horrified and cried, "You will destroy our whole family!"

sentences.zh: 神色為之不寧者數日。

translations.literal: His expression was unsettled for several days.
translations.idiomatic: For days his face showed nothing but agitation.

sentences.zh: 策，敦煌人。

translations.literal: Ce was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ce was from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 光逢，隱之子也。

translations.literal: Guangfeng was the son of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guangfeng was the son of Yin.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使劉仁恭，驕侈貪暴，常慮幽州城不固，築館於大安山，曰：「此山四面懸絕，可以少制眾。」

translations.literal: The Lulong military governor Liu Rengong was arrogant, extravagant, greedy, and cruel. He often worried that Youzhou city was not secure and built a lodge on Mount Da'an, saying, "This mountain is sheer on all sides; a few can control the many."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong, military governor of Lulong, was arrogant, extravagant, greedy, and brutal. Uneasy about the defenses of Youzhou, he built a palace on Mount Da'an, saying, "These cliffs drop away on every side—a handful of men can hold off a multitude."

sentences.zh: 其棟宇壯麗，擬於帝者。

translations.literal: Its halls were magnificent, rivaling an emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: Its halls were built on an imperial scale.

sentences.zh: 選美女實其中。

translations.literal: He selected beautiful women to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: He stocked them with beautiful women.

sentences.zh: 與方士煉丹藥，求不死。

translations.literal: With Daoist masters he refined elixirs, seeking not to die.
translations.idiomatic: He worked with Daoist adepts refining elixirs in search of immortality.

sentences.zh: 悉斂境內錢，瘞於山顛；

translations.literal: He collected all money within his borders and buried it on the mountain peak;
translations.idiomatic: He seized every coin in his territory and buried it on the summit;

sentences.zh: 令民間用堇泥為錢。

translations.literal: he ordered the people to use clay for money.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered the common people to use lumps of clay as currency.

sentences.zh: 又禁江南茶商無得入境，自采山中草木為茶，鬻之。

translations.literal: He also forbade Jiangnan tea merchants from entering his borders and gathered mountain plants himself to make and sell tea.
translations.idiomatic: He barred Jiangnan tea merchants from his domain, harvested wild plants from the mountains, and sold the brew himself.

sentences.zh: 仁恭有愛妾羅氏，其子守光通焉。

translations.literal: Rengong had a favorite concubine, Lady Luo; his son Shouguang had relations with her.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong kept a favorite concubine, Lady Luo, with whom his son Shouguang had an affair.

sentences.zh: 仁恭杖守光而斥之，不以為子數。

translations.literal: Rengong beat Shouguang and drove him off, no longer counting him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong thrashed Shouguang and cast him out, disowning him.

sentences.zh: 李思安引兵入其境，所過焚蕩無餘。

translations.literal: Li Si'an led troops into his territory; wherever they passed they burned and ravaged without leaving anything.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'an invaded his territory and left nothing standing wherever his columns passed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己酉，直抵幽州城下。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jiyou, he reached directly below Youzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Jiyou, he marched straight to the walls of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁恭猶在大安山。

translations.literal: Rengong was still on Mount Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong was still on Mount Da'an.

sentences.zh: 城中無備，幾至不守。

translations.literal: The city had no defense and nearly could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: The city was undefended and nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 守光自外引兵入，登城拒守；

translations.literal: Shouguang led troops in from outside, mounted the wall, and held the defense;
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang brought troops in from outside, climbed the walls, and organized the defense;

sentences.zh: 又出兵與思安戰，思安敗退。

translations.literal: he also sent troops out to fight Si'an, and Si'an was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: then sent a sortie against Si'an, who was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 守光遂自稱節度使，命部將李小喜、元行欽將兵攻大安山。

translations.literal: Shouguang then declared himself military governor and ordered his subordinates Li Xiaoxi and Yuan Xingqin to lead troops against Mount Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang thereupon proclaimed himself military governor and ordered his officers Li Xiaoxi and Yuan Xingqin to march on Mount Da'an.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遣兵拒戰，為小喜所敗。

translations.literal: Rengong sent troops to resist; they were defeated by Xiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong sent troops to meet them and was routed by Xiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 虜仁恭以歸，囚於別室。

translations.literal: They captured Rengong and brought him back, imprisoning him in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Rengong, brought him back, and locked him in a side chamber.

sentences.zh: 仁恭將佐及左右，凡守光素所惡者皆殺之。

translations.literal: Rengong's aides and attendants—everyone Shouguang had long hated—were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Every aide and attendant Rengong had relied on—anyone Shouguang had long despised—was put to death.

sentences.zh: 銀胡□錄都指揮使王思同帥部兵三千，山後八安巡檢使李承約帥部兵二千奔河東，守光弟守奇奔契丹，未幾，亦奔河東，河東節度使晉王克用以承約為匡霸指揮使，思同為飛騰指揮使。

translations.literal: The Yinhu Lu regiment commander Wang Sitong led three thousand of his troops; the Shanhou Ba'an inspector Li Chengyue led two thousand of his and fled to Hedong. Shouguang's brother Shouqi fled to the Khitan; before long he too fled to Hedong. The Hedong military governor, Prince of Jin Li Keyong, made Chengyue commander of Kuangba and Sitong commander of Feiteng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sitong, commander of the Yinhu Lu regiment, led three thousand of his men; Li Chengyue, Ba'an inspector of the Shanhou region, led two thousand of his—and both fled to Hedong. Shouguang's brother Shouqi fled to the Khitan, then soon followed them to Hedong. Li Keyong, Prince of Jin and military governor of Hedong, appointed Chengyue commander of Kuangba and Sitong commander of Feiteng.

sentences.zh: 思同母，仁恭之女也。

translations.literal: Sitong's mother was Rengong's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong's mother was Rengong's daughter.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，梁王始御金祥殿，受百官稱臣，下書稱教令，自稱曰寡人。

translations.literal: On the day Gengxu the Prince of Liang first took the Jinxiang Hall, received the hundred officials' obeisance as subjects, issued documents styled as edicts, and referred to himself as "I, the One of Little Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengxu the Prince of Liang first occupied the Jinxiang Hall, received the officials' homage as their sovereign, issued orders styled as imperial edicts, and called himself "I, of little virtue."

sentences.zh: 辛亥，令諸箋、表、簿、籍皆去唐年號，但稱月、日。

translations.literal: On the day Xinhai he ordered that all memorials, reports, registers, and records remove the Tang reign title and give only month and day.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinhai he decreed that every memorial, report, ledger, and register drop the Tang reign era and mark only month and day.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，張文蔚等至大梁。

translations.literal: On the day Bingchen, Zhang Wenwei and the others reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Bingchen, Zhang Wenwei and his party arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 盧佶聞錢傳鐐等將至，將水軍拒之於青澳。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhe heard that Qian Chuanliao and the others were coming, he led his fleet to block them at Qing'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Qian Chuanliao was on his way, Lu Zhe took the fleet to intercept him at Qing'ao.

sentences.zh: 錢傳瓘曰：「佶之精兵盡在於此，不可與戰。」

translations.literal: Qian Chuanjin said, "Zhe's crack troops are all here; we must not fight them."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chuanjin said, "Zhe has committed his best troops here—we must not engage them."

sentences.zh: 乃自安固捨舟，間道襲溫州。

translations.literal: He then left the boats at Angu, took hidden paths, and raided Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the boats at Angu, struck overland by secret routes, and stormed Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，溫州潰，擒佶斬之。

translations.literal: On the day Wuwu, Wenzhou collapsed; they captured Zhe and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuwu the city fell; they seized Zhe and executed him.

sentences.zh: 吳王鏐以都監使吳璋為溫州制置使，命傳瓘等移兵討盧約於處州。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Qian Liu appointed Wu Zhang military commissioner of Wenzhou and ordered Chuanjin and the others to move their forces to attack Lu Yue at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Qian Liu installed Wu Zhang as commissioner over Wenzhou and ordered Chuanjin and the rest to shift their campaign against Lu Yue at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，梁王更名晃。

translations.literal: On the day Renxu the Prince of Liang changed his name to Huang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renxu the Prince of Liang changed his name to Huang.

sentences.zh: 王兄全昱聞王將即帝位，謂王曰：「朱三，爾可作天子乎！」

translations.literal: The Prince's elder brother Quanxu heard that the Prince was about to become emperor and said to him, "Zhu the Third, can you really be Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Quanxu, learning that he was about to take the throne, said to him, "Zhu the Third—do you honestly think you can be Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 甲子，張文蔚、楊涉乘輅自上源驛從冊寶，諸司各備儀衛鹵簿前導，百官從其後，至金祥殿前陳之。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi, Zhang Wenwei and Yang She rode in the imperial carriage from the Shangyuan post station with the investiture regalia; each office prepared ceremonial guards and insignia to lead the way, and the hundred officials followed behind to the front of the Jinxiang Hall and arrayed them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiazi, Zhang Wenwei and Yang She rode in the imperial carriage from Shangyuan Station bearing the regalia of investiture; every bureau mustered its ceremonial guards and insignia to go before them, the officials following, until they reached the Jinxiang Hall and set everything in place.

sentences.zh: 王被兗冕，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The Prince donned the imperial cap and robes and ascended as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince put on the imperial cap and robes and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 張文蔚、蘇循奉冊升殿進讀，楊涉、張策、薛貽矩、趙光逢以次奉寶升殿，讀已，降，帥百官舞蹈稱賀。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun bore the document up the hall and read it; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng in turn bore the treasures up the hall. When the reading was finished they descended, and led the hundred officials in bowing and congratulatory dance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun carried the investiture scroll up the hall and read it aloud; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng followed with the imperial treasures. When the rites were done they came down and led the officials in the congratulatory prostration.

sentences.zh: 帝遂與文蔚等宴於玄德殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor then feasted with Wenwei and the others in the Xuande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor then banqueted Wenwei and the others in the Xuande Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝舉酒曰：「朕輔政未久，此皆諸公推戴之力。」

translations.literal: The Emperor raised his cup and said, "I have assisted in government only a short while; all this is the power of your urging."
translations.idiomatic: Raising his cup, the Emperor said, "I have governed only briefly; this is entirely your doing in pressing me forward."

sentences.zh: 文蔚等皆慚懼，俯伏不能對，獨蘇循、薛貽矩及刑部尚書張禕盛稱帝功德宜應天順人。

translations.literal: Wenwei and the others were all ashamed and afraid, bowed low and could not answer; only Su Xun, Xue Yiju, and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi loudly praised the Emperor's merit as fitting Heaven and following the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei and the rest were mortified and dumb, prostrate and speechless; only Su Xun, Xue Yiju, and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi loudly proclaimed that his merit matched Heaven and accorded with the people's will.

sentences.zh: 帝復與宗戚飲博於宮中，酒酣，朱全昱忽以投瓊擊盆中迸散，睨帝曰：「朱三，汝本碭山一民也，從黃巢為盜，天子用汝為四鎮節度使，富貴極矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor again drank and gambled with his clansmen in the palace. When the wine was deep, Zhu Quanxu suddenly hurled his gaming piece and struck the bowl, scattering it. He glared at the Emperor and said, "Zhu the Third, you were originally a commoner of Dangshan, followed Huang Chao as a bandit, and the Son of Heaven used you as military governor of four circuits until your wealth and honor reached their limit!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went on drinking and dicing with his kinsmen inside the palace. Deep in his cups, Quanxu suddenly flung his gambling counter, smashed the dish, and glared at him: "Zhu the Third, you were a peasant from Dangshan who ran with Huang Chao as a bandit. The Tang Son of Heaven made you governor of four circuits—you had wealth and honor enough!

sentences.zh: 奈何一旦滅唐家三百年社稷，自稱帝王！

translations.literal: Why in a single morning destroy the Tang house's three-hundred-year altars and call yourself emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Why in one morning destroy the Tang altars of three hundred years and style yourself emperor?

sentences.zh: 行當族滅，奚以博為！」

translations.literal: You are about to have your clan exterminated—what is there to gamble for!"
translations.idiomatic: Your whole clan will be wiped out—what do you have left to wager?"

sentences.zh: 帝不懌而罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and dismissed the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took offense and broke up the party.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，命有司告天地、宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: On the day Yichou he ordered the authorities to announce to Heaven, Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yichou he ordered the rites announced to Heaven, Earth, the imperial ancestors, and the state altars.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，遣使宣諭州、鎮。

translations.literal: On the day Dingmao he sent envoys to proclaim the change to the prefectures and circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Dingmao he dispatched envoys to notify every prefecture and circuit.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，大赦，改元，國號大梁。

translations.literal: On the day Wuchen he proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the reign title, and the state was named Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuchen he declared a general amnesty, adopted a new reign era, and named the dynasty Great Liang.

sentences.zh: 奉唐昭宣帝為濟陰王，皆如前代故事，唐中外舊臣官爵並如故。

translations.literal: The Tang Emperor Zhaoxuan was honored as Prince of Jiyin, all following the precedents of former dynasties; Tang officials within and without kept their ranks and titles as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaoxuan of Tang was styled Prince of Jiyin under the old dynastic precedents, and Tang officials at court and in the provinces retained their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 以汴州為開封府，命曰東都；

translations.literal: Bianzhou was made the Kaifeng Prefecture and called the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Bianzhou became Kaifeng Prefecture and was named the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 以故東都為西都；

translations.literal: the former Eastern Capital was made the Western Capital;
translations.idiomatic: the old Eastern Capital was redesignated the Western Capital;

sentences.zh: 廢故西京，以京兆府為大安府，置佑國軍於大安府，更名魏博曰天雄軍。

translations.literal: the former Western Capital was abolished; Jingzhao Prefecture was made Da'an Prefecture; the Youguo Army was stationed at Da'an; and Weibo was renamed the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: the former Western Capital was abolished; Jingzhao became Da'an Prefecture with the Youguo Army garrisoned there; and Weibo was retitled the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 遷濟陰王於曹州，栫之以棘，使甲士守之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiyin was moved to Caozhou, fenced in with thorns, and guarded by armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Tang ruler was transferred to Caozhou, penned in with thorn hedges, and watched by armed guards.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以武安節度使馬殷為楚王。

translations.literal: On the day Xinwei, the Wuan military governor Ma Yin was made Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinwei, Ma Yin, military governor of Wuan, was created Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 以宣武掌書記、太府卿敬翔知崇政院事，以備顧問，參謀議，於禁中承上旨，宣於宰相而行之。

translations.literal: The Xuanwu chief clerk and Grand Steward Jing Xiang was made director of the Chongzheng Court to advise and deliberate; in the palace he received the Emperor's will and conveyed it to the chancellors for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang, chief clerk of Xuanwu and Grand Steward of the Imperial Treasury, was named director of the Chongzheng Court to counsel the throne; inside the palace he took the Emperor's orders and transmitted them to the chancellors for action.

sentences.zh: 宰相非進對時有所奏請及已受旨應復請者，皆具記事因崇政院以聞，得旨則復宣於宰相。

translations.literal: When chancellors who were not in audience wished to memorialize or, having received an order, needed to memorialize again, they all wrote the matter down and reported it through the Chongzheng Court; when they received assent they again conveyed it to the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever chancellors not in direct audience needed to submit business—or needed to confirm an order already received—they recorded it and sent it through the Chongzheng Court; once approved, the director relayed the decision back to them.

sentences.zh: 翔為人沉深，有智略，在幕府三十餘年，軍謀、民政，帝一以委之。

translations.literal: Xiang was deep and reserved, full of strategy; for more than thirty years in the staff headquarters military plans and civil administration were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was grave, shrewd, and far-sighted; for over thirty years in the Prince's service every military and civil matter passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 翔盡心勤勞，晝夜不寐，自言惟馬上乃得休息，帝性暴戾難近，人莫能測，惟翔能識其意趣。

translations.literal: Xiang gave his heart to tireless labor, day and night without sleep, saying that only on horseback could he rest. The Emperor's nature was violent and hard to approach; none could fathom him—only Xiang could read his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He drove himself without sleep, claiming he could rest only in the saddle. The Emperor was savage and unpredictable; no one else could read him—only Xiang knew what he meant.

sentences.zh: 或有所不可，翔未嘗顯言，但微示持疑；

translations.literal: When something was not acceptable, Xiang never spoke plainly but only subtly showed doubt;
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor erred, Xiang never rebuked him openly but hinted his misgivings;

sentences.zh: 帝意已悟，多為之改易。

translations.literal: the Emperor's mind would already understand and he often changed course for Xiang's sake.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor usually grasped the hint and altered course.

sentences.zh: 禪代之際，翔謀居多。

translations.literal: At the time of the abdication Xiang's plotting was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: During the transfer of the mandate, Xiang's counsel weighed most heavily.

sentences.zh: 追尊皇高祖考、妣以來皆為帝、後，皇考誠為烈祖文穆皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his great-grandparents and all forebears as emperors and empresses; his father was honored as Emperor Liezu, posthumous name Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his ancestors from the great-grandfather down to imperial rank; his father was canonized as Emperor Liezu Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 妣王氏為文惠皇后。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Wang, was honored as Empress Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Wang, became Empress Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 初，帝為四鎮節度使，凡倉庫之籍，置建昌院以領之；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor was military governor of four circuits, all warehouse registers were placed under the Jianchang Court to administer;
translations.idiomatic: When he still governed four circuits, every warehouse ledger had been run through the Jianchang Court;

sentences.zh: 至是，以養子宣武節度副使友文為開封尹、判院事，掌凡國之金谷。

translations.literal: now his adopted son, Xuanwu deputy military governor Youwen, was made prefect of Kaifeng and director of the court, in charge of all state revenues.
translations.idiomatic: now his adopted son Youwen, deputy governor of Xuanwu, was named prefect of Kaifeng and director of the court, controlling the empire's finances.

sentences.zh: 友文本康氏之子也。

translations.literal: Youwen was originally the son of the Kang family.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen had been born to the Kang clan.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，下制削奪李克用官爵。

translations.literal: On the day Yihai an edict stripped Li Keyong of rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yihai an edict degraded Li Keyong and stripped his offices.

sentences.zh: 是時，惟河東、鳳翔、淮南稱「天祐」，西川稱「天復」年號。

translations.literal: At this time only Hedong, Fengxiang, and Huainan used the reign title "Tianyou"; Xichuan used "Tianfu."
translations.idiomatic: “Only Hedong, Fengxiang, and Huainan still dated their calendars as Tianyou; Sichuan kept Tianfu.”

sentences.zh: 餘皆稟梁正朔，稱臣奉貢。

translations.literal: The rest all followed Liang's calendar, submitted as subjects, and sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Every other region accepted Liang's calendar, acknowledged subject status, and paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 蜀王與弘農王移檄諸道，云欲與岐王、晉王會兵興復唐室，卒無應者。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu and the Prince of Hongnong sent proclamations to the circuits saying they wished to join the Prince of Qi and the Prince of Jin in arms to restore the Tang house, but in the end none answered.
translations.idiomatic: The rulers of Shu and Hongnong issued manifestos to the provinces, calling for an alliance with Qi and Jin to restore Tang—but no one responded.

sentences.zh: 蜀王乃謀稱帝，下教諭統內吏民；

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu then plotted to declare himself emperor and issued an edict instructing officials and people within his domain;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu then planned to take the throne and issued orders to his officials and people;

sentences.zh: 又遺晉王書云：「請各帝一方，俟朱溫既平，乃訪唐宗室立之，退歸籓服。」

translations.literal: he also wrote to the Prince of Jin, saying, "Let each of us reign in his own region. After Zhu Wen is overthrown we shall seek a Tang imperial clansman to enthrone, then return to our feudal duties."
translations.idiomatic: and wrote to the Prince of Jin: "Let each reign in his own quarter. Once Zhu Wen falls we will find a Tang prince to restore, then return to our posts as vassals."

sentences.zh: 晉王復書不許，曰：「誓於此生靡敢失節。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin replied refusing, saying, "I swear that in this life I dare not break my loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin refused: "I have sworn never in this life to break faith with Tang."

sentences.zh: 唐末之誅宦官也，詔書至河東，晉王匿監軍張承業於斛律寺，斬罪人以應詔。

translations.literal: When the Tang at its end executed the eunuchs, the edict reached Hedong; the Prince of Jin hid the army supervisor Zhang Chengye in the Hulu Temple and beheaded criminals to satisfy the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the late Tang purged the eunuchs, the edict reached Hedong; the Prince of Jin hid army supervisor Zhang Chengye in Hulu Temple and executed condemned men to satisfy the court.

sentences.zh: 至是，復以為監軍，待之加厚，承業亦為之竭力。

translations.literal: Now he restored Chengye as supervisor and treated him still more generously; Chengye also served him with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Now he restored Chengye to his post and treated him even more generously; Chengye repaid him with total loyalty.

sentences.zh: 岐王治軍甚寬，待士卒簡易。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi governed the army very leniently and treated soldiers in an easy, familiar way.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi ran his army loosely and dealt with his men informally.

sentences.zh: 有告部將苻昭反者，岐王直詣其家，悉去左右，熟寢經宿而還；

translations.literal: When someone reported that a subordinate commander, Fu Zhao, was rebelling, the Prince went straight to his house, dismissed all attendants, and slept soundly there overnight before returning;
translations.idiomatic: When he was told that Fu Zhao was plotting rebellion, he went to Fu's house alone, sent away every guard, and slept the night through before returning;

sentences.zh: 由是眾心悅服。

translations.literal: from this the hearts of the masses were won.
translations.idiomatic: after that his men trusted him utterly.

sentences.zh: 然御軍無紀律。

translations.literal: Yet he had no military discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet discipline in his ranks was lax.

sentences.zh: 及聞唐亡，以兵羸地蹙，不敢稱帝，但開岐王府，置百官，名其所居為宮殿，妻稱皇后，將吏上書稱箋表，鞭、扇、號令多擬帝者。

translations.literal: When he heard the Tang had perished, his troops were weak and his territory cramped, and he did not dare call himself emperor; he only opened the Qi Prince's mansion, set up the hundred offices, named his residence a palace, his wife a queen, and his officers submitted memorials styled as petitions; whips, fans, and orders largely imitated an emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Tang's fall, with weak armies and a cramped domain he stopped short of claiming the throne; instead he opened a princely court, styled his home a palace and his wife a queen, and let his officers use imperial forms—whips, fans, and commands all mimicked a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鎮海節度判官羅隱說吳王鏐興兵討梁，曰：「縱無成功，猶可退保杭、越，自為東帝；

translations.literal: Luo Yin, military judge of Zhenhai, urged Prince of Wu Qian Liu to raise troops against Liang, saying, "Even if you do not succeed, you can still fall back on Hang and Yue and be an eastern emperor yourself;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yin, judge on Qian Liu's staff, urged the Prince of Wu to march against Liang: "Even if you fail, you can still hold Hang and Yue and rule the east as your own emperor;

sentences.zh: 奈何交臂事賊，為終古之羞乎！」

translations.literal: why fold your arms and serve the bandit, a shame for all ages!"
translations.idiomatic: why surrender to the usurper and earn eternal infamy?"

sentences.zh: 鏐始以隱為不遇於唐，必有怨心，及聞其言，雖不能用，心甚義之。

translations.literal: Liu had thought Yin, having failed to advance under Tang, must harbor resentment; when he heard this he could not adopt it but greatly respected his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had assumed Yin, passed over by Tang, nursed a grudge; hearing this he could not act on it but admired the man's courage.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁丑朔，以御史大夫薛貽矩為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day Dingchou of the month, Xue Yiju was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day Dingchou, Xue Yiju was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-equal chancellor.

sentences.zh: 加武順軍節度使趙王王鎔守太師，天雄節度使鄴王羅紹威守太傅，義武節度使王處直兼侍中。

translations.literal: The Wushun military governor, Prince of Zhao Wang Rong, was advanced to Grand Preceptor; the Tianxiong military governor, Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei, to Grand Tutor; the Yiwu military governor Wang Chuzhi was concurrently made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Prince of Zhao and governor of Wushun, was promoted to Grand Preceptor; Luo Shaowei, Prince of Ye and governor of Tianxiong, to Grand Tutor; Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu was made Palace Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣其臣袍笏梅老來通好，帝遣太府少卿高頎報之。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent their minister Paochameilao to seek friendship; the Emperor sent Vice Director of the Grand Treasury Gao Yin to respond.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Minister Paochameilao to open relations; the Emperor sent Vice Director of the Grand Treasury Gao Yin in reply.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹有八部，部各有大人，相與約，推一人為王，建旗鼓以號令諸部，每三年則以次相代。

translations.literal: Earlier the Khitan had eight tribes, each with its own chief; they agreed to choose one man as king, raise banners and drums to command the tribes, and every three years pass the kingship in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan once comprised eight tribes, each with a chief; they agreed to elect one king, raise banners and drums to command all, and rotate the kingship every three years.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，有習爾者為王，土宇始大。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiantong era Xier became king and their territory first grew large.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Xiantong, Xier became king and their domain first expanded.

sentences.zh: 其後欽德為王，乘中原多故，時入盜邊。

translations.literal: Later Qinde became king; taking advantage of turmoil in the central plains he often raided the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qinde reigned and, exploiting chaos in China, repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及阿保機為王，尤雄勇，五姓奚及七姓室韋、達靼咸役屬之。

translations.literal: When Abaoji became king he was especially bold; the five Xi surnames and seven Shiwei surnames, and the Tatars, all became his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: When Abaoji took the throne he was fiercer still; the five Xi clans, seven Shiwei clans, and Tatars all submitted.

sentences.zh: 阿保機姓邪律氏，恃其強，不肯受代。

translations.literal: Abaoji bore the surname Yelü; relying on his strength he refused to accept rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji of the Yelü clan refused rotation, trusting in his power.

sentences.zh: 久之，阿保機擊黃頭室韋還，七部劫之於境上，求如約。

translations.literal: After a long while, when Abaoji returned from attacking the Yellow-head Shiwei, the seven tribes seized him on the border and demanded fulfillment of the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, returning from a campaign against the Yellow-head Shiwei, the seven tribes intercepted him at the frontier and demanded he honor the pact.

sentences.zh: 阿保機不得已，傳旗鼓，且曰：「我為王九年，得漢人多，請帥種落居古漢城，與漢人守之，別自為一部。」

translations.literal: Abaoji had no choice; he passed on the banners and drums and said, "I have been king nine years and gained many Han people. Let me lead my tribe to dwell at the old Han city and guard it with the Han, forming a separate tribe of my own."
translations.idiomatic: Forced to comply, he surrendered the banners and drums, saying, "Nine years I have ruled and gathered many Han subjects. Let me settle my people at the old Han city to guard it with them as a separate tribe."

sentences.zh: 七部許之。

translations.literal: The seven tribes consented.
translations.idiomatic: The seven tribes agreed.

sentences.zh: 漢城者，故後魏滑鹽縣也。

translations.literal: The Han city was the old Northern Wei county of Huayan.
translations.idiomatic: That "Han city" was the former Northern Wei county of Huayan.

sentences.zh: 地宜五穀，有鹽池之利。

translations.literal: The land suited the five grains and had the advantage of salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: Its soil grew grain, and its salt pans brought wealth.

sentences.zh: 其後阿保機稍以兵擊滅七部，復並為一國。

translations.literal: Later Abaoji gradually used troops to destroy the seven tribes and reunite them into one state.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji then campaigned against the seven tribes until he destroyed them and united the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 又北侵室韋、女真，西取突厥故地，擊奚，滅之，復立奚王而使契丹監其兵，東北諸夷皆畏服之。

translations.literal: He also invaded north into Shiwei and Jurchen, west into old Turk lands, attacked and destroyed the Xi, reinstalled a Xi king but set Khitan overseers over his troops, and the northeastern tribes all feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He marched north against Shiwei and Jurchen, west into former Turk domains, crushed the Xi and reinstalled their king under Khitan officers, until every tribe of the northeast bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，阿保機帥眾三十萬寇雲州，晉王與之連和，面會東城，約為兄弟，延之帳中，縱酒，握手盡歡，約以今冬共擊梁。

translations.literal: That year Abaoji led three hundred thousand men to raid Yun Prefecture. The Prince of Jin allied with him, met him face to face at the eastern wall, became sworn brothers, entertained him in his tent with free drinking, clasped hands in full joy, and agreed to strike Liang together that winter.
translations.idiomatic: That year Abaoji led three hundred thousand men against Yun Prefecture. The Prince of Jin allied with him, met him east of the city, swore brotherhood, feasted him in his tent, and pledged a joint attack on Liang that winter.

sentences.zh: 或勸晉王：「因其來，可擒也，」王曰：「仇敵未滅而失信夷狄，自亡之道也。」

translations.literal: Some urged the Prince of Jin, "Since he has come, you could seize him." The Prince said, "With our foe not yet destroyed, to break faith with the barbarians is the road to self-destruction."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged the Prince of Jin to seize him while he was there. He replied, "Our chief enemy still stands—if we betray the Khitan now we invite our own ruin."

sentences.zh: 阿保機留旬日乃去，晉王贈以金繒數萬。

translations.literal: Abaoji stayed more than ten days before leaving; the Prince of Jin gave him tens of thousands in gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji lingered ten days, then departed; the Prince of Jin sent him lavish gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 阿保機留馬三千匹，雜畜萬計以酬之。

translations.literal: Abaoji left three thousand horses and tens of thousands of mixed livestock in return.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji left three thousand horses and myriad livestock in exchange.

sentences.zh: 阿保機既歸而背盟，更附於梁，晉王由是而恨之。

translations.literal: After Abaoji returned he broke the alliance and turned to Liang; the Prince of Jin therefore came to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: Once home, however, Abaoji broke faith and sided with Liang, and the Prince of Jin never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以河南尹兼河陽節度使張全義為魏王；

translations.literal: On the day Jimao, the Henan prefect and concurrent Heyang military governor Zhang Quanyi was made Prince of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jimao, Zhang Quanyi, prefect of Henan and military governor of Heyang, was created Prince of Wei;

sentences.zh: 鎮海、鎮東節度使吳王錢鏐為吳越王；

translations.literal: the Zhenhai and Zhendong military governor, Prince of Wu Qian Liu, was made Prince of Wuyue;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, Prince of Wu and governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong, was created Prince of Wuyue;

sentences.zh: 加清海節度使劉隱、威武節度使王審知兼侍中，乃以隱為大彭王。

translations.literal: the Qinghai military governor Liu Yin and the Weiwu military governor Wang Shenzhi were concurrently made Palace Attendants, and Yin was further made Prince of Dapeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin of Qinghai and Wang Shenzhi of Weiwu were made Palace Attendants, and Yin was also created Prince of Dapeng.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以權知荊南留後高季昌為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day Guiwei, Gao Jichang, acting military commissioner of Jingnan, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guiwei, Gao Jichang, acting commissioner of Jingnan, received full appointment as governor.

sentences.zh: 荊南舊統八州，乾符以來，寇亂相繼，諸州皆為鄰道所據，獨餘江陵。

translations.literal: Jingnan had formerly governed eight prefectures; since the Qianfu era successive raids and rebellions left every prefecture taken by neighboring circuits, and only Jiangling remained.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan once held eight prefectures, but since Qianfu bandits and rebels had stripped all but Jiangling, each lost to a neighbor.

sentences.zh: 季昌到官，城邑殘毀，戶口雕耗。

translations.literal: When Jichang took office the city was in ruins and the population depleted.
translations.idiomatic: When Jichang arrived the walls were shattered and the people scattered.

sentences.zh: 季昌安集流散，民皆復業。

translations.literal: Jichang settled the displaced and the people all returned to their trades.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the refugees, and the populace returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，立皇兄全昱為廣王，子友文為博王，友珪為郢王，友璋為福王，友貞為均王，友雍為賀王，友徽為建王。

translations.literal: On the day Yiyou he enfeoffed his elder brother Quanxu as Prince of Guang, his son Youwen as Prince of Bo, Yougui as Prince of E, Youzhang as Prince of Fu, Youzhen as Prince of Jun, Youyong as Prince of He, and Youhui as Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiyou he enfeoffed his brother Quanxu as Prince of Guang and his sons Youwen, Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, and Youhui as princes of Bo, E, Fu, Jun, He, and Jian.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以東都舊第為建昌宮，改判建昌院事為建昌宮使。

translations.literal: On the day Xinmao the old eastern capital residence was made the Jianchang Palace, and the director of the Jianchang Court was renamed director of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinmao the former eastern residence became the Jianchang Palace, and its director was retitled palace superintendent.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，命保平節度使康懷貞將兵八萬會魏博兵攻潞州。

translations.literal: On the day Renchen he ordered the Baoping military governor Kang Huaizhen to lead eighty thousand troops to join the Weibo army in attacking Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renchen he ordered Kang Huaizhen of Baoping to march eighty thousand men with the Weibo force against Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔廢樞密院，其職事皆入於崇政院，以知院事敬翔為院使。

translations.literal: On the day Jiawu an edict abolished the Bureau of Military Affairs; its duties all entered the Chongzheng Court, and Jing Xiang, director of the court, was made court superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiawu the Bureau of Military Affairs was abolished and its powers folded into the Chongzheng Court; Jing Xiang became its superintendent.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書蘇循及其子起居郎楷自謂有功於梁，當不次擢用；

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Su Xun and his son, Attendant of the Heir Apparent Su Kai, considered themselves meritorious in Liang's founding and due for extraordinary promotion;
translations.idiomatic: Su Xun, Minister of Rites, and his son Kai, an attendant of the heir apparent, believed they had earned extraordinary promotion in founding Liang;

sentences.zh: 循朝夕望為相，帝薄其為人，敬翔及殿中監李振亦鄙之。

translations.literal: Xun morning and evening looked to become chancellor, but the Emperor despised his character, and Jing Xiang and Palace Director Li Zhen also scorned him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun daily expected the chancellorship, but the Emperor despised him, as did Jing Xiang and Palace Director Li Zhen.

sentences.zh: 翔言於帝曰：「蘇循，唐之鴟梟，賣國求利，不可以立於惟新之朝。」

translations.literal: Xiang said to the Emperor, "Su Xun is the owl of Tang, who sold the state for profit and cannot stand in a court of renewal."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang told the Emperor, "Su Xun is Tang's carrion bird—he sold his dynasty for gain and has no place in a new court."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔循及刑部尚書張禕等十五人並勒致仕，楷斥歸田里。

translations.literal: On the day Wuxu an edict ordered Xun and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi and fifteen others all compelled to retire; Kai was expelled to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuxu an edict forced Xun, Zhang Yi, and fifteen others to retire; Kai was banished to his native place.

sentences.zh: 循父子乃之河中依朱友謙。

translations.literal: Father and son then went to Hezhong to rely on Zhu Youqian.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son fled to Hezhong and placed themselves under Zhu Youqian.

sentences.zh: 盧約以處州降吳越。

translations.literal: Lu Yue surrendered Chuzhou to Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yue surrendered Chuzhou to Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 弘農王以鄂岳觀察使劉存為西南面都招討使，岳州刺史陳知新為岳州團練使，廬州觀察使劉威為應援使，別將許玄應為監軍，將水軍三萬以擊楚。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hongnong appointed the E-Yue observation commissioner Liu Cun supreme commander of the southwest, the Yue prefecture training commissioner Chen Zhixin training commissioner of Yue, the Luzhou observation commissioner Liu Wei relief commander, and another commander Xu Xuanying supervisor of the army, and led thirty thousand naval troops to attack Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hongnong named Liu Cun, observation commissioner of E-Yue, supreme commander of the southwest; Chen Zhixin, training commissioner of Yue; Liu Wei of Luzhou as relief commander; Xu Xuanying as army supervisor—and sent thirty thousand sailors against Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚王馬殷甚懼，靜江軍使楊定真賀曰：「我軍勝矣！」

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Ma Yin was greatly afraid. The Jingjiang army commissioner Yang Dingzhen congratulated him, saying, "Our army will win!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chu Ma Yin was terrified. Yang Dingzhen, commissioner of the Jingjiang army, congratulated him: "We are going to win!"

sentences.zh: 殷問其故，定真曰：「夫戰懼則勝，驕則敗。

translations.literal: Yin asked the reason. Dingzhen said, "In battle, fear brings victory and arrogance brings defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yin asked why. Dingzhen said, "In war, fear wins and arrogance loses.

sentences.zh: 今淮南兵直趨吾城，是驕而輕敵也；

translations.literal: Now the Huainan army is marching straight on our city—that is arrogance and despising the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan host is driving straight for our walls—that is arrogance and contempt for us;

sentences.zh: 而王有懼色，吾是以知其必勝也。」

translations.literal: yet Your Highness shows fear, and therefore I know we must win."
translations.idiomatic: yet you, my lord, are afraid—and that is why we will prevail."

sentences.zh: 殷命在城都指揮使秦彥暉將水軍三萬浮江而下，水軍副指揮使黃璠帥戰艦三百屯瀏陽口。

translations.literal: Yin ordered the city commander Qin Yanhui to lead thirty thousand naval troops downriver; the deputy naval commander Huang Fan led three hundred warships to anchor at Liuyang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Yin ordered Qin Yanhui, commander in the capital, to sail thirty thousand men downriver, while Huang Fan with three hundred warships blocked Liuyang Ford.

sentences.zh: 六月，存等遇大雨，引兵還至越堤北，彥暉追之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Cun and the others met heavy rain, led their troops back north of the Yue embankment, and Yanhui pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Cun's fleet was caught in storms, retreated north of the Yue dike, and Yanhui gave chase.

sentences.zh: 存數戰不利，乃遺殷書詐降。

translations.literal: After several battles without success, Cun sent Yin a letter feigning surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats Cun wrote Yin offering a false surrender.

sentences.zh: 彥暉使謂殷曰：「此必詐也，勿受！」

translations.literal: Yanhui had someone tell Yin, "This must be a trick—do not accept it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui warned Yin, "This is surely a ruse—do not accept!"

sentences.zh: 存與彥暉夾水而陣，存遙呼曰：「殺降不祥，公獨不為子孫計耶！」

translations.literal: Cun and Yanhui arrayed their forces on opposite banks. Cun called across the water, "To kill those who surrender is unlucky—will you not think of your descendants!"
translations.idiomatic: They formed battle lines on opposite shores. Cun shouted across the water, "Slaying men who yield brings ill fortune—have you no care for your sons and grandsons?"

sentences.zh: 彥暉曰：「賊入吾境而不擊，奚顧子孫！」

translations.literal: Yanhui said, "Bandits enter our borders and we do not strike—why care about descendants!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui answered, "Enemies invade our land and you want mercy—what descendants?"

sentences.zh: 鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: He beat the drums and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He drummed the charge and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 存等走，黃璠自瀏陽引兵絕江，與彥暉合擊，大破之，執存及知新，裨將死者百餘人，士卒死者以萬數，獲戰艦八百艘。

translations.literal: Cun and the others fled. Huang Fan led troops from Liuyang across the river, joined Yanhui in a combined attack, and routed them utterly. They captured Cun and Zhixin; more than a hundred subordinate commanders died, soldiers died by the tens of thousands, and eight hundred warships were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Cun's force broke. Fan crossed from Liuyang, joined Yanhui, and crushed them. Cun and Zhixin were taken; over a hundred officers and tens of thousands of soldiers died; eight hundred ships were captured.

sentences.zh: 威以餘眾遁歸，彥暉遂拔岳州。

translations.literal: Wei fled home with the remnant troops, and Yanhui then took Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei escaped with the survivors while Yanhui seized Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 殷釋存、知新之縛，慰諭之。

translations.literal: Yin released Cun and Zhixin from their bonds and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yin freed Cun and Zhixin and tried to win them over.

sentences.zh: 二人皆罵曰：「丈夫以死報主，肯事賊乎！」

translations.literal: The two cursed, saying, "A man dies to serve his lord—would we serve bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Both cursed him: "Men die for their masters—we will never serve a traitor!"

sentences.zh: 遂斬之。

translations.literal: They were then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They were executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 許玄應，弘農王之腹心也，常預政事，張顥、徐溫因其敗，收斬之。

translations.literal: Xu Xuanying was the Prince of Hongnong's intimate and often took part in government. Zhang Hao and Xu Wen used his defeat as the occasion to seize and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuanying, a confidant who often shaped policy, was seized and killed by Zhang Hao and Xu Wen after the defeat.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷遣兵會吉州刺史彭玕攻洪州，不克。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Yin sent troops to join the Jizhou military governor Peng Qian in attacking Hong Prefecture but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin sent forces with Peng Qian, governor of Jizhou, against Hong Prefecture but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 康懷貞至潞州，晉昭義節度使李嗣昭、副使李嗣弼閉城拒守。

translations.literal: Kang Huaizhen reached Lu Prefecture; the Jin Zhaoyi military governor Li Sizhao and his deputy Li Sibi closed the city and held out.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Huaizhen reached Lu Prefecture; Li Sizhao, Jin governor of Zhaoyi, and his deputy Li Sibi shut the gates and resisted.

sentences.zh: 懷貞晝夜攻之，半月不克，乃築壘穿蚰蜓塹而守之，內外斷絕。

translations.literal: Huaizhen attacked day and night; after half a month without success he built ramparts and cut a winding trench to besiege it, cutting off inside from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen assaulted without pause; after half a month he threw up walls and dug a serpentine trench to starve the city, severing it from the world.

sentences.zh: 晉王以蕃、漢都指揮使周德威為行營都指揮使，帥馬軍都指揮使李嗣本、馬步都虞候李存璋、先鋒指揮使史建瑭、鐵林都指揮使安元信、橫衝指揮使李嗣源、騎將安金全救潞州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin appointed the Han and tribal commander Zhou Dewei supreme commander of the campaign army, leading the horse army commander Li Siben, the horse-and-foot inspector Li Cunzhang, vanguard commander Shi Jiantang, Iron Forest commander An Yuanxin, Crossbolt commander Li Siyuan, and cavalry general An Jinquan to rescue Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin named Zhou Dewei, commander of Han and tribal forces, supreme commander of the relief army, with Li Siben, Li Cunzhang, Shi Jiantang, An Yuanxin, Li Siyuan, and An Jinquan to save Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嗣弼，克修之子；

translations.literal: Sibi was the son of Ke Xiu;
translations.idiomatic: Sibi was a son of Li Kexiu;

sentences.zh: 嗣本，本姓張；

translations.literal: Siben was originally surnamed Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: Siben had been born a Zhang.

sentences.zh: 建瑭，敬思之子；

translations.literal: Jiantang was the son of Jingsi;
translations.idiomatic: Jiantang was Jingsi's son.

sentences.zh: 金全，代北人也。

translations.literal: Jinquan was a man from north of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan came from the northern frontier country of Dai.

sentences.zh: 晉兵攻澤州，帝遣左神勇軍使范居實將兵救之。

translations.literal: Jin troops attacked Ze Prefecture; the Emperor sent the Left Divine Valor Army commissioner Fan Jushi to lead troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin forces besieged Ze Prefecture, the Emperor dispatched Fan Jushi of the Left Divine Valor Army with a relief column.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以平盧節度使韓建守司徒、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day Jiayin, Pinglu military governor Han Jian was appointed acting Grand Mentor and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Han Jian, governor of Pinglu, was made acting Grand Mentor and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 武貞節度使雷彥恭會楚兵攻江陵，荊南節度使高季昌引兵屯公安，絕其糧道；

translations.literal: Wuzhen military governor Lei Yangan joined Chu troops in attacking Jiangling; Jingnan military governor Gao Jichang led troops to encamp at Gong'an and cut off their supply route;
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yangan of Wuzhen allied with Chu forces against Jiangling, but Gao Jichang of Jingnan marched to Gong'an and severed their line of supply;

sentences.zh: 彥恭敗，楚兵亦走。

translations.literal: Yangan was defeated, and the Chu troops also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yangan was routed and the Chu army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉守光既囚其父，自稱盧龍留後，遣使請命。

translations.literal: After Liu Shouguang had imprisoned his father, he styled himself acting governor of Lulong and sent envoys to request confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Shouguang had locked up his father, he proclaimed himself acting governor of Lulong and petitioned the court for recognition.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午，以守光為盧龍節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiawu, Shouguang was appointed military governor of Lulong and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiawu, Shouguang received the posts of military governor of Lulong and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 靜海節度使曲裕卒，丙申，以其子權知留後顥為節度使。

translations.literal: Jinghai military governor Qu Yu died; on the day Bingshen, his son Quan, acting governor, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yu, governor of Jinghai, died; on bingshen his son Quan, who had been acting governor, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 雷彥恭攻岳州，不克。

translations.literal: Lei Yangan attacked Yue Prefecture but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yangan assaulted Yue Prefecture without success.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙午，賜河南尹張全義名宗奭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day Bingwu, the Emperor bestowed on Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi the name Zongyi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the eighth month, the Emperor granted Zhang Quanyi, intendant of Henan, the honorific name Zongyi.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以吳越王鏐兼淮南節度使，楚王殷兼武昌節度使，各充本道招討制置使。

translations.literal: On the day Xinhai, the King of Wuyue, Qian Liu, was additionally made military governor of Huainan, and the King of Chu, Ma Yin, was additionally made military governor of Wuchang; each was also appointed supreme commander and commissioner for pacification of his own circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Qian Liu of Wuyue and Ma Yin of Chu were given concurrent governorships of Huainan and Wuchang respectively, along with full authority as circuit pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 晉周德威壁於高河，康懷貞遣親騎都頭秦武將兵擊之，武敗。

translations.literal: Jin's Zhou Dewei fortified at Gaohe; Kang Huaizhen sent his personal cavalry commander Qin Wu to attack him, and Wu was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei of Jin held Gaohe; Kang Huaizhen sent his elite cavalry chief Qin Wu against him, and Wu was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 丁已，帝以亳州刺史李思安代懷貞為潞州行營都統，黜懷貞為行營都虞候。

translations.literal: On the day Dingsi, the Emperor replaced Huaizhen with Bozhou governor Li Si'an as supreme commander of the Lu Prefecture campaign army and demoted Huaizhen to deputy supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Emperor relieved Kang Huaizhen of supreme command at Lu Prefecture, naming Li Si'an of Bozhou in his place and reducing Huaizhen to second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 思安將河北兵西上，至潞州城下，更築重城，內以防奔突，外以拒援兵，謂之夾寨。

translations.literal: Si'an led Hebei troops westward to the foot of Lu Prefecture's walls and built another heavy walled camp—within to guard against sallies, without to block relief troops—called the Twin Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an marched his Hebei army to Lu Prefecture and threw up a second walled ring: an inner line against breakout, an outer line against relief—the Twin Stockade.

sentences.zh: 調山東民饋軍糧，德威日以輕騎抄之，思安乃自東南山口築甬道，屬於夾寨。

translations.literal: He requisitioned grain from the people of Shandong to feed the army; Dewei daily sent light cavalry to raid the convoys, so Si'an built a covered causeway from the southeastern mountain pass linking to the Twin Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: With Shandong levies hauling provisions, Dewei harried the supply trains daily with light horse; Si'an then drove a covered passage from the southeastern pass into the Twin Stockade.

sentences.zh: 德威與諸將互往攻之，排牆填塹，一晝夜間數十發，梁兵疲於奔命。

translations.literal: Dewei and the other generals took turns attacking it, tearing down walls and filling ditches—several dozen assaults in a single day and night—and the Liang troops were worn out racing to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei and his commanders hammered the works in rotation, breaching walls and filling trenches in dozens of attacks within a day and night, until the Liang soldiers could barely keep pace.

sentences.zh: 夾寨中出芻牧者，德威輒抄之，於是梁兵閉壁不出。

translations.literal: Whenever fodder-gatherers or herdsmen came out of the Twin Stockade, Dewei would raid them; thus the Liang army shut the gates and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei seized every party that ventured out for fodder or pasture, until the Liang garrison dared not open its gates.

sentences.zh: 九月，雷彥恭攻涔陽、公安，高季昌擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Lei Yangan attacked Cenyang and Gong'an; Gao Jichang defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Lei Yangan struck Cenyang and Gong'an; Gao Jichang repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 彥恭貪殘類其父，專以焚掠為事，荊、湖間常被其患；

translations.literal: Yangan was greedy and cruel like his father, devoting himself solely to burning and plunder; the Jing and Hu regions were often afflicted by him;
translations.idiomatic: Yangan matched his father's greed and cruelty, living by fire and loot; Jing and the lake country suffered him again and again;

sentences.zh: 又附於淮南。

translations.literal: he also attached himself to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: and he threw in his lot with Huainan.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔削彥恭官爵，命季昌與楚王殷討之。

translations.literal: On the day Bingshen, an edict stripped Yangan of rank and titles and ordered Jichang and King Yin of Chu to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the court degraded Yangan and charged Gao Jichang and King Yin of Chu to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 蜀王會將佐議稱帝，皆曰：「大王雖忠於唐，唐已亡矣，此所謂『天與不取』者也。」

translations.literal: The King of Shu convened his staff to discuss assuming the imperial title; all said, "Your Highness has been loyal to Tang, but Tang is already gone—this is what is called 'Heaven offers and you do not take.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian of Shu gathered his counselors to proclaim an empire; all urged him: "You have served Tang faithfully, yet Tang is no more—this is the gift Heaven sets before you and you refuse."

sentences.zh: 馮涓獨獻議，請以蜀王稱制，曰：「朝興則未爽稱臣，賊在則不同為惡。」

translations.literal: Feng Juan alone offered a plan, asking that the King of Shu assume regency, saying, "When the court flourishes, we have not yet lightly styled ourselves subjects; while the bandit remains, we do not share his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Only Feng Juan dissented, proposing that Wang Jian rule as regent: "While the legitimate house still stands we need not rush to call ourselves its servants; so long as the usurper endures we must not be counted among his kind."

sentences.zh: 王不從，涓杜門不出。

translations.literal: The King did not follow him; Juan shut his door and would not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian rejected the advice; Feng Juan closed his gates and withdrew from court.

sentences.zh: 王用安撫副使、掌書記韋莊之謀，帥吏民哭三日；

translations.literal: The King, using the plan of Pacification Deputy Commissioner and chief secretary Wei Zhuang, led officials and people in three days of mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Following Wei Zhuang, his pacification deputy and chief secretary, Wang led officials and commoners in three days of lamentation for the fallen dynasty;

sentences.zh: 己亥，即皇帝位，國號大蜀。

translations.literal: on the day Jihai, he ascended the imperial throne; the state was named Great Shu.
translations.idiomatic: on jihai he took the throne as emperor, founding the state of Great Shu.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以前東川節度使兼侍中王宗佶為中書令，韋莊為左散騎常侍、判中書門下事，閬州防禦使唐道襲為內樞密使。

translations.literal: On the day Xinchou, the former Dongchuan military governor and Palace Attendant Wang Zongjie was made Director of the Secretariat; Wei Zhuang was made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant and Controller of the Secretariat and Chancellery; Langzhou defense commissioner Tang Daoxi was made Inner Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Wang Zongjie, former governor of Dongchuan, became Director of the Secretariat; Wei Zhuang became Left Regular Cavalry Attendant with control of the Secretariat and Chancellery; Tang Daoxi of Langzhou became Inner Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 莊，見素之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhuang was the grandson of Jian Su.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was a grandson of the Tang minister Wei Jian Su.

sentences.zh: 蜀主雖目不知書，好與書生談論，粗曉其理。

translations.literal: Although the Shu sovereign could not read by sight, he loved to converse with scholars and roughly understood their reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Though illiterate by the bookman's standard, the Shu emperor delighted in talk with literati and grasped their arguments well enough.

sentences.zh: 是時唐衣冠之族多避亂在蜀，蜀主禮而用之，使修舉故事，故其典章文物有唐之遺風。

translations.literal: At that time many families of Tang official rank had fled the turmoil into Shu; the Shu sovereign treated them with ceremony and employed them, having them restore old precedents, so that its institutions and ritual objects preserved Tang's lingering style.
translations.idiomatic: Scores of Tang gentry had sought refuge in Shu; Wang Jian honored and used them to revive court ritual, so that Shu law and ceremony still breathed the air of Tang.

sentences.zh: 蜀主長子校書郎宗仁幼以疾廢，立其次子秘書少監宗懿為遂王。

translations.literal: The Shu sovereign's eldest son, proofreader Wang Zongren, had been disabled by illness in youth; he established his second son, Secretariat Vice-Director Zongyi, as Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zongren, a proofreader, had been crippled by illness in boyhood; he named his second son Zongyi, Secretariat Vice-Director, Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，高季昌遣其將倪可福會楚將秦彥暉攻朗州，雷彥恭遣使乞降於淮南，且告急。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Gao Jichang sent his general Ni Kefu to join the Chu general Qin Yanhui in attacking Lang Prefecture; Lei Yangan sent envoys to surrender to Huainan and also to plead for aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Gao Jichang sent Ni Kefu with the Chu commander Qin Yanhui against Langzhou; Lei Yangan sued for peace with Huainan and begged for rescue.

sentences.zh: 弘農王遣將泠業將水軍屯平江，李饒將步騎屯瀏陽以救之，楚王殷遣岳州刺史許德勳將兵拒之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hongnong sent his general Leng Ye to lead the water army to encamp at Pingjiang, and Li Rao to lead foot and horse to encamp at Liuyang to save him; King Yin of Chu sent Yue Prefecture governor Xu Deqin with troops to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo of Hongnong dispatched Leng Ye's fleet to Pingjiang and Li Rao's combined force to Liuyang; King Yin of Chu sent Xu Deqin, governor of Yue, to block them.

sentences.zh: 泠業進屯朗口，德勳使善游者五十人，以木枝葉覆其首，持長刀浮江而下，夜犯其營，且舉火，業軍中驚擾。

translations.literal: Leng Ye advanced to encamp at Langkou; Deqin sent fifty skilled swimmers who covered their heads with branches and leaves, held long knives, and floated down the river by night to strike his camp, also setting fires; Ye's army was thrown into alarm and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ye moved up to Langkou; Deqin floated fifty swimmers downstream at night, heads camouflaged with foliage and long knives in hand, to storm the camp and light fires until Ye's host dissolved in panic.

sentences.zh: 德以大軍進擊，大破之，追至鹿角鎮，擒業；

translations.literal: Deqin then advanced with the main army and inflicted a great defeat, pursuing to Lucheng Fort and capturing Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Deqin followed with his main force, shattered the enemy, ran them down to Lucheng Fort, and took Ye prisoner;

sentences.zh: 又破瀏陽寨，擒李饒；

translations.literal: he also broke the Liuyang stockade and captured Li Rao;
translations.idiomatic: he overran the Liuyang camp as well and seized Li Rao;

sentences.zh: 掠上高、唐年而歸。

translations.literal: then plundered Shanggao and Tangnian and returned.
translations.idiomatic: then raided Shanggao and Tangnian before marching home.

sentences.zh: 斬業、饒於長沙市。

translations.literal: Ye and Rao were beheaded in the market at Changsha.
