translations.idiomatic: Ye and Rao were executed in the Changsha marketplace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲申，夾馬指揮使尹皓攻晉江豬嶺寨，拔之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day Jiashen, the Jia Ma commander Yin Hao attacked the Jin stockade at River Boar Ridge and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, Yin Hao of the Jia Ma command seized the Jin outpost at River Boar Ridge.

sentences.zh: 義昌節度使劉守文聞其弟守光幽其父，集將吏大哭曰：「不意吾家生此梟獍！

translations.literal: Yichang military governor Liu Shouwen, hearing that his younger brother Shouguang had imprisoned their father, gathered his generals and officials and wept aloud, saying, "I never thought our house would breed such an owl and jackal!
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouwen of Yichang learned that Shouguang had caged their father, he summoned his officers and wailed: "That our line should produce such a monster—I never dreamed it!

sentences.zh: 吾生不如死，誓與諸君討之！」

translations.literal: I would rather live than die; I swear with you all to punish him!"
translations.idiomatic: Better dead than living with this shame; I vow to march with you against him!"

sentences.zh: 乃發兵擊守光，互有勝負。

translations.literal: He then raised troops to attack Shouguang; each side had victories and defeats.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field against Shouguang, and the brothers traded blows without a clear victor.

sentences.zh: 天雄節度使鄴王紹威謂其下曰：「守光以窘急歸國，守文孤立無援，滄州可不戰服也。」

translations.literal: Tianxiong military governor Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei said to his subordinates, "Shouguang has returned to the empire in dire straits; Shouwen stands alone without aid—Cangzhou can be made to submit without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei, Prince of Ye and governor of Tianxiong, told his staff: "Shouguang has come home desperate; Shouwen is isolated—Cangzhou ought to yield without a battle."

sentences.zh: 乃遺守文書，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: He then sent Shouwen a letter expounding fortune and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Shouwen a letter laying out ruin and reward.

sentences.zh: 守文亦恐梁乘虛襲其後，戊子，遣使請降，以子延祐為質。

translations.literal: Shouwen also feared that Liang might seize the chance to strike his rear; on the day Wuzi, he sent envoys to request surrender, offering his son Yanyou as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen likewise dreaded a Liang strike from behind; on wuzi he sued for terms and sent his son Yanyou as hostage.

sentences.zh: 帝拊手曰：「紹威折簡，勝十萬兵！」

translations.literal: The Emperor clapped his hands and said, "Shaowei's folded letter is worth a hundred thousand troops!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor struck his palms and cried, "One letter from Shaowei outweighs a hundred thousand spears!

sentences.zh: 加守文中書令，撫納之。

translations.literal: Shouwen was additionally made Director of the Secretariat and treated with kindness and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and received with honor.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在籓鎮，用法嚴，將校有戰沒者，所部兵悉斬之，謂之跋隊斬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor was in his frontier command, he applied the law severely: whenever a commander died in battle, all troops of his unit were beheaded—called decapitating the rear ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In his days as a frontier lord the Emperor had ruled with iron severity: if a commander fell, every soldier of his command was executed—the practice known as decapitating the rear ranks.

sentences.zh: 士卒失主將者，多亡逸不敢歸。

translations.literal: Soldiers who had lost their commanding general mostly fled and dared not return.
translations.idiomatic: Men whose officers had been killed mostly deserted and never dared go home.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命凡軍士皆文其面以記軍號。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered that all soldiers be tattooed on the face to record their army designation.
translations.idiomatic: He then decreed that every soldier bear on his face the mark of his unit.

sentences.zh: 軍士或思鄉里逃去，關津輒執之送所屬，無不死者，其鄉里亦不敢容。

translations.literal: When soldiers thought of home and fled, the passes and fords would seize them and send them back to their unit—none escaped death; their home districts also dared not shelter them.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters were seized at every pass and returned to face execution; their villages would not hide them.

sentences.zh: 由是亡者皆聚山澤為盜，大為州縣之患。

translations.literal: Thus the fugitives all gathered in mountains and marshes as bandits, becoming a great affliction to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives therefore banded in hills and swamps, plaguing the countryside.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，詔赦其罪，自今雖文面亦聽還鄉里。

translations.literal: On the day Renyin, an edict pardoned their crimes; from now on, even if tattooed they were permitted to return to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin an amnesty forgave them; hereafter even the branded might go home.

sentences.zh: 盜減什七八。

translations.literal: Banditry was reduced by seven or eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Robbery fell by seven or eight parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 淮南右都押牙米志誠等將兵渡淮襲穎州，克其外郭。

translations.literal: Huainan's Right Commissioner of Military Control Mi Zhicheng and others led troops across the Huai to raid Ying Prefecture and captured its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Zhicheng of Huainan's right military commission crossed the Huai, stormed Yingzhou, and took the outer city.

sentences.zh: 刺史張實據子城拒守。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Shi held the inner citadel and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Shi barricaded himself in the inner keep.

sentences.zh: 晉王命李存璋攻晉州，以分上黨兵勢。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin ordered Li Cunzhang to attack Jin Prefecture to divide the Shangdang army's strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin sent Li Cunzhang against Jin Prefecture to draw off the Shangdang siege force.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬戌，詔河中、陝州發兵救之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day Renxu, an edict ordered Hezhong and Shaan Prefectures to dispatch troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the twelfth month the court ordered Hezhong and Shaan to march to its relief.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔發步騎五千救穎州，米志誠等引去。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi, an edict ordered five thousand foot and horse to rescue Ying Prefecture; Mi Zhicheng and the others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi five thousand infantry and cavalry were sent to Yingzhou; Mi Zhicheng pulled back.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，晉兵寇洺州。

translations.literal: On the day Dingmao, Jin troops raided Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Jin forces struck Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淮南兵攻信州，刺史危仔倡求救於吳越。

translations.literal: Huainan troops attacked Xin Prefecture; governor Wei Zichang requested aid from Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan besieged Xinzhou; Governor Wei Zichang appealed to Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸酉朔，蜀主登興義樓。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day Guiyou of the new year, the Shu sovereign ascended the Tower of Rising Fortune.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the New Year's day guiyou, the Shu emperor mounted the Tower of Rising Fortune.

sentences.zh: 有僧抉一目以獻，蜀主命飯僧萬人以報之。

translations.literal: A monk gouged out one eye to present it; the Shu sovereign ordered ten thousand monks fed in recompense.
translations.idiomatic: A monk plucked out an eye as an offering; the emperor commanded that ten thousand monks be fed in return.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士張格曰：「小人無故自殘，赦其罪已幸矣，不宜復崇獎以敗風俗。」

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Zhang Ge said, "For a petty man to mutilate himself without cause—pardoning his crime is already mercy enough; he should not be further honored and rewarded to corrupt custom.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin scholar Zhang Ge protested: "Wanton self-mutilation deserves no praise—pardoning him is grace enough; to reward it would poison the manners of the realm."

sentences.zh: 蜀主乃止。

translations.literal: The Shu sovereign then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，蜀以韋莊為門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day Dingchou, Shu appointed Wei Zhuang Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Wei Zhuang was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，蜀主祀南郊；

translations.literal: On the day Xinsi, the Shu sovereign sacrificed at the Southern Suburb;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the Shu emperor offered at the Southern Altar;

sentences.zh: 壬午，大赦，改元武成。

translations.literal: on the day Renwu, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: on renwu he proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 晉王疽發於首，病篤。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin had a carbuncle break out on his head; his illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: An abscess opened on the Prince of Jin's head and his sickness turned critical.

sentences.zh: 周德威等退屯亂柳。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei and the others withdrew to encamp at Luanliu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei and his commanders fell back to Luanliu.

sentences.zh: 晉王命其弟內外蕃漢都知兵馬使、振武節度使克寧、監軍張承業、大將李存璋、吳珙、掌書記盧質立其子晉州刺史存勖為嗣，曰：「此子志氣遠大，必能成吾事，爾曹善教導之！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin ordered his younger brother, the Inner and Outer Han-and-Tribal Commissioner of Military Affairs and Zhenwu military governor Kening, the army supervisor Zhang Chengye, the great generals Li Cunzhang and Wu Gong, and chief secretary Lu Zhi to establish his son, Jin Prefecture governor Cunxu, as heir, saying, "This boy's spirit is far-reaching; he will surely accomplish my enterprise—you must all teach and guide him well!
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong named his brother Kening, Zhang Chengye, Li Cunzhang, Wu Gong, and Lu Zhi to install his son Cunxu, governor of Jinzhou, as heir: "The lad's ambition runs deep—he will finish what I began; see that you school him well!"

sentences.zh: 辛卯，晉王謂存勖曰：「嗣昭厄於重圍，吾不及見矣。

translations.literal: On the day Xinmao, the Prince of Jin said to Cunxu, "Sizhao is trapped in heavy siege—I shall not live to see him freed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he told Cunxu, "Sizhao is locked in a ring of iron—I will not see him rescued.

sentences.zh: 俟葬畢，汝與德威輩速竭力救之！」

translations.literal: When the burial is complete, you and Dewei and the rest must swiftly exert all your strength to save him!"
translations.idiomatic: After my rites, you and Dewei must bend every force to break him free!"

sentences.zh: 又謂克寧等曰：「以亞子累汝！」

translations.literal: He also said to Kening and the others, "I leave the burden of the Heir Apparent upon you!
translations.idiomatic: To Kening and the rest he said, "The boy is your charge now!"

sentences.zh: 亞子，存勖小名也。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent was Cunxu's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent" had been Cunxu's pet name since boyhood.

sentences.zh: 言終而卒。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke no more and died.

sentences.zh: 克寧綱紀軍府，中外無敢喧嘩。

translations.literal: Kening held the military administration in order; within and without, none dared make an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Kening kept the headquarters in firm discipline; inside and out, no one dared stir.

sentences.zh: 克寧久總兵柄，有次立之勢，時上黨圍未解，軍中以存勖年少，多竊議者，人情忷忷。

translations.literal: Kening had long held military power and had the standing of one next to succeed; at that time the Shangdang siege was not yet lifted, and in the army many whispered because Cunxu was young—the mood was uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Kening had commanded for years and stood as the obvious alternate heir; with Shangdang still besieged and Cunxu barely grown, the camps murmured and hearts were unsettled.

sentences.zh: 存勖懼，以位讓克寧。

translations.literal: Cunxu was afraid and offered the position to Kening.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu, in fear, offered Kening the throne.

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「汝冢嗣也，且有先王之命，誰敢違之！」

translations.literal: Kening said, "You are the legitimate heir, and there is moreover the late king's command—who would dare disobey!
translations.idiomatic: Kening refused: "You are the named heir and hold your father's dying charge—who would defy that?

sentences.zh: 將吏欲謁見存勖，存勖方哀哭未出。

translations.literal: The generals and officials wished to pay their respects to Cunxu, but Cunxu was still wailing in mourning and had not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Officers came to bow to Cunxu, but he remained indoors in mourning and would not appear.

sentences.zh: 張承業入謂存勖曰：「大孝在不墜基業，多哭何為！」

translations.literal: Zhang Chengye entered and said to Cunxu, "The greatest filial piety lies in not letting the enterprise fall; what use is so much weeping!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengyei entered and said, "True filial piety is to keep the realm from crumbling—not to drown it in tears!

sentences.zh: 因扶存勖出，襲位為河東節度使、晉王。

translations.literal: He thereupon supported Cunxu out; Cunxu succeeded to the posts of Hedong military governor and Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He led Cunxu forth; Cunxu assumed the governorship of Hedong and the title Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 李克寧首帥諸將拜賀，王悉以軍府事季之。

translations.literal: Li Kening was first among the generals to bow in congratulation; the Prince entrusted him with all military administration affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kening led the commanders in homage, and the new prince placed the whole military administration in his hands.

sentences.zh: 以李存璋為河東軍城使、馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: Li Cunzhang was made Hedong fortress commander and horse-and-foot inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunzhang was appointed commander of the Hedong citadel and inspector of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 先王之時，多寵借胡人及軍士，侵擾市肆，存璋既領職，執其尤暴橫者戮之，旬月間城中肅然。

translations.literal: In the late king's time, many barbarians and soldiers had been indulged in harassing the markets; once Cunzhang took office, he seized the most violent and arrogant and executed them; within a ten-day month the city was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Under the late king, favored tribesmen and soldiers had bullied the markets at will; Cunzhang took office, seized the worst offenders, and put them to death—in a fortnight the capital was quiet.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐遣兵攻淮南甘露鎮，以救信州。

translations.literal: The King of Wuyue, Qian Liu, sent troops to attack Huainan's Ganlu garrison to rescue Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu of Wuyue marched on Huainan's Ganlu post to relieve Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀中書令王宗佶，於諸假子為最長，且恃其功，專權驕恣。

translations.literal: Shu's Director of the Secretariat Wang Zongjie was eldest among the adopted sons and, relying on his achievements, monopolized power in arrogance and license.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongjie, Shu Director of the Secretariat, was the eldest of the adopted sons; bloated by his deeds, he ruled by arrogance.

sentences.zh: 唐道襲已為樞密使，宗佶猶以名呼之；

translations.literal: Tang Daoxi was already Privy Commissioner, yet Zongjie still called him by his personal name;
translations.idiomatic: Though Tang Daoxi had become Privy Commissioner, Zongjie still addressed him familiarly by name;

sentences.zh: 道襲心銜之而事之逾謹。

translations.literal: Daoxi harbored resentment in his heart yet served him with still greater deference.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi nursed the insult yet served him all the more scrupulously.

sentences.zh: 宗佶多樹黨友，蜀主亦惡之。

translations.literal: Zongjie cultivated many partisan friends; the Shu sovereign also detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjie packed the court with his creatures, and the emperor came to loathe him.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲辰，以宗佶為太師，罷政事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day Jiachen, Zongjie was made Grand Preceptor and removed from government.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the second month Zongjie was elevated to Grand Preceptor and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 蜀以戶部侍郎張格為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Shu appointed Revenue Vice-Minister Zhang Ge Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Shu named Zhang Ge of the Revenue Ministry Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 格為相，多迎合主意；

translations.literal: As chancellor, Ge mostly catered to the sovereign's wishes;
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Zhang Ge trimmed his sails to the emperor's mood;

sentences.zh: 有勝己者，必以計排去之。

translations.literal: whoever surpassed him, he was sure to scheme and drive away.
translations.idiomatic: any rival he contrived to ruin and remove.

sentences.zh: 初，晉王克用多養軍中壯士為子，寵遇如真子。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Jin Li Keyong had often taken stalwart men from the army as adopted sons, favoring them like true sons.
translations.idiomatic: In his prime Li Keyong had adopted many of the army's fiercest warriors as sons, treating them as his own.

sentences.zh: 及晉王存勖立，諸假子皆年長握兵，心怏怏不服，或托疾不出，或見新王不拜。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin Li Cunxu was established, all the adopted sons were grown and held troops; their hearts were sullen and unwilling to submit—some pleaded illness and would not come out, some saw the new king and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cunxu succeeded, the adopted sons were grown commanders with armies at their backs; they seethed in resentment—some feigned sickness, some refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 李克寧權位既重，人情多向之。

translations.literal: Li Kening's power and position were already weighty, and popular sentiment mostly inclined toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kening's authority was heavy, and more than a few hearts already turned his way.

sentences.zh: 假子李存顥陰說克寧曰：「兄終弟及，自古有之。

translations.literal: The adoptive son Li Cunhao secretly urged Kening, saying: "When an elder brother dies, the younger brother succeeds him—this has been so since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunhao, one of the adoptive sons, secretly pressed Li Kening: "Brother succeeds brother when the elder dies—that is as old as rule itself.

sentences.zh: 以叔拜侄，於理安乎！

translations.literal: For an uncle to bow to his nephew—is that reasonable in principle!
translations.idiomatic: How can it be right in principle for an uncle to bow to his nephew!

sentences.zh: 天與不取，後悔無及！」

translations.literal: When Heaven offers it and you do not take it, you will regret it beyond remedy!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven offers you the throne—refuse it, and regret will come too late!"

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「吾家世以慈孝聞天下，先王之業苟有所歸，吾復何求！

translations.literal: Kening said: "Our house has been known throughout the realm for kindness and filial piety generation after generation. If the former king's enterprise has someone to whom it may pass, what more do I seek!
translations.idiomatic: Li Kening replied, "Our clan has been famed across the realm for kindness and filial piety for generations. If the late king's legacy already has a rightful heir, what more could I want?

sentences.zh: 汝勿妄言，我且斬汝！」

translations.literal: Do not speak recklessly—I shall cut you down first!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not talk nonsense, or I will cut you down myself!"

sentences.zh: 克寧妻孟氏，素剛悍，諸假子各遣其妻入說孟氏，孟氏以為然，且慮語洩及禍，數以迫克寧。

translations.literal: Kening's wife Lady Meng, who was by nature fierce and overbearing, had each of the other adoptive sons send his wife in to persuade Lady Meng. She thought the plan sound and, fearing that word would leak out and bring disaster, repeatedly pressed Kening.
translations.idiomatic: Kening's wife, Lady Meng, was fierce and domineering by nature. The other adoptive sons each sent their wives to win her over; she agreed with the plot and, fearing exposure and ruin, pressed Kening again and again.

sentences.zh: 克寧性怯，朝夕惑於眾言，心不能無動；

translations.literal: Kening was timid by nature; day and night he was swayed by everyone's talk, and his heart could not remain unmoved;
translations.idiomatic: Timid by nature, Kening was pulled this way and that by the talk around him day and night, and his heart could not stay still;

sentences.zh: 又與張承業、李存璋相失，數誚讓之；

translations.literal: moreover he had fallen out with Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang and repeatedly berated them;
translations.idiomatic: he had also broken with Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang and repeatedly abused them;

sentences.zh: 又因事擅殺都虞候李存質；

translations.literal: he also on one pretext or another executed on his own authority the commander of military police Li Cunzhi;
translations.idiomatic: and on one excuse or another he had executed on his own authority the commander of military police, Li Cunzhi;

sentences.zh: 又求領大同節度使，以蔚、朔、應州為巡屬。

translations.literal: and he further asked to take charge as military governor of Datong, with Yu, Shuo, and Ying prefectures as his circuit oversight.
translations.idiomatic: he further asked to be made military governor of Datong, with Yu, Shuo, and Ying as prefectures under his command.

sentences.zh: 晉王皆聽之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin granted him everything.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin granted every request.

sentences.zh: 李存顥等為克寧謀，因晉王過其第，殺承業、存璋，奉克寧為節度使，舉河東九州附於梁，執晉王及太夫人曹氏送大梁。

translations.literal: Li Cunhao and the others plotted for Kening: when the Prince of Jin passed his residence, they would kill Chengye and Cunzhang, install Kening as military governor, submit all nine prefectures of Hedong to Liang, seize the Prince of Jin and Lady Dowager Cao, and send them to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunhao and his party plotted for Kening: when the Prince of Jin came to his house, they would kill Chengye and Cunzhang, set Kening up as military governor, hand all nine Hedong prefectures to Liang, seize the prince and Lady Dowager Cao, and send them to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 太原人史敬鎔，少事晉王克用，居帳下，見親信，克寧欲知府中陰事，召敬鎔，密以謀告之。

translations.literal: Shi Jingrong of Taiyuan had served Prince Jin Keyong from youth, living in his tent entourage and regarded as trusted. Kening wished to learn the mansion's secret affairs, summoned Jingrong, and confided the plot to him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingrong of Taiyuan had served Prince Jin Keyong since youth in the tent guard and was counted among the trusted. Kening wanted to know what was going on inside the residence, summoned Jingrong, and told him the plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 敬鎔陰許之，入告太夫人，太夫人大駭，召張承業，指晉王謂之曰：「先王把此兒臂授公等，如聞外間謀欲負之，但置吾母子有地，勿送大梁，自它不以累公。」

translations.literal: Jingrong feigned agreement in secret, went in and told the Lady Dowager. She was greatly alarmed, summoned Zhang Chengye, pointed at the Prince of Jin and said to him: "The late king placed this boy's arm in your hands. If you hear that outsiders are plotting to betray him, only see that my son and I have somewhere to stand—do not send us to Daliang—and beyond that I will not involve you."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong pretended to agree, then went in and told the lady dowager. She was terrified and summoned Zhang Chengye. Pointing at the Prince of Jin, she said, "The late king placed this boy's arm in your hands. If you hear outsiders plotting against him, only give my son and me somewhere to live—do not send us to Daliang—and I will not burden you further."

sentences.zh: 承業惶恐曰：「老奴以死奉先王之命，此何言也！」

translations.literal: Chengye said in panic: "This old slave will obey the late king's command unto death—what words are these!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye said in alarm, "This old slave will die carrying out the late king's command—what talk is this!"

sentences.zh: 晉王以克寧之謀告，且曰：「至親不可自相魚肉，吾苟避位，則亂不作矣。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin told Chengye of Kening's plot and also said: "Close kin must not devour one another like fish and flesh. If I simply yield my place, the disorder will not arise."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin told Chengye of Kening's plot and added, "Close kin must not tear one another apart. If I step aside, the turmoil will never start."

sentences.zh: 承業曰：「克寧欲投大王母子於虎口，不除之豈有全理！」

translations.literal: Chengye said: "Kening wishes to cast Your Highness and your mother into the tiger's maw—if he is not removed, how can there be any prospect of safety!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye said, "Kening means to throw you and your mother to the tiger—unless he is removed, how can you be safe?"

sentences.zh: 乃召李存璋、吳珙及假子李存敬、長直軍使朱守殷，使陰為之備。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Li Cunzhang, Wu Gong, the adoptive son Li Cunjing, and the commander of the long-service guard Zhu Shouyin, and had them secretly make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Li Cunzhang, Wu Gong, the adoptive son Li Cunjing, and Zhu Shouyin, commander of the long-service guard, and had them prepare in secret.

sentences.zh: 壬戍，置酒會諸將於府捨，伏甲執克寧、存顥於座。

translations.literal: On the day Renshu they set out wine and gathered the generals at the mansion residence; armed men lying in wait seized Kening and Cunhao in their seats.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Renshu they set out wine and gathered the generals at the residence; men with weapons hidden in wait seized Kening and Cunhao at the table.

sentences.zh: 晉王流涕數之曰：「兒郎勖以軍府讓叔父，叔父不取。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, weeping, rebuked them: "Your nephew Xun offered you the military government; you would not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin wept as he rebuked them: "Your nephew Xun offered you the command of the army, and you would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 今事已定，奈何復為此謀，忍以吾母子遺仇讎乎！」

translations.literal: Now the affair is settled—why plot thus again, and bear to hand my mother and me over to our enemies!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that everything is settled, why plot again and hand my mother and me over to our enemies!"

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「此皆讒人交構，夫復何言！」

translations.literal: Kening said: "These are all slanderers weaving intrigue—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Kening said, "Slanderers have set this up—what more can I say!"

sentences.zh: 是日，殺克寧及存顥。

translations.literal: That same day they executed Kening and Cunhao.
translations.idiomatic: That day they executed Kening and Cunhao.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，鴆殺濟陰王於曹州，追謚曰唐哀皇帝。

translations.literal: On the day Guihai they poisoned the Prince of Jiyin at Caozhou; posthumously he was given the temple name Tang Aidi ("Lamented Emperor of Tang").
translations.idiomatic: On the day Guihai they poisoned the Prince of Jiyin at Caozhou and gave him the posthumous title Tang Aidi, Lamented Emperor of Tang.

sentences.zh: 甲子，蜀兵入歸州，執刺史張瑭。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi Shu troops entered Guizhou and captured the prefect Zhang Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiazi Shu forces entered Guizhou and seized the prefect Zhang Tang.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以韓建為侍中，兼建昌宮使。

translations.literal: On the day Xinwei Han Jian was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinwei Han Jian was made Palace Attendant and concurrently commissioner of the Jianchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 李思安等攻潞州，久不下，士卒疲弊，多逃亡。

translations.literal: Li Si'an and the others besieged Luzhou for a long time without taking it; the soldiers were worn out and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'an and his command had attacked Luzhou for a long time without success; the troops were exhausted and desertions were many.

sentences.zh: 晉兵猶屯余吾寨，帝疑晉王克用詐死，欲召兵還，恐晉人躡之，乃議自至澤州應接歸師，且召匡國節度使劉知俊將兵趣澤州。

translations.literal: Jin troops were still encamped at the Yuyu stockade. The Emperor suspected that Prince Jin Keyong had feigned death; he wished to recall his army but feared Jin forces would pursue. He therefore discussed going in person to Zezhou to meet and escort the returning troops, and also summoned Liu Zhijun, military governor of Kuangguo, to lead troops toward Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops were still at the Yuyu stockade. The emperor suspected Prince Jin Keyong had faked his death. He wanted to pull the army back but feared pursuit, so he considered going to Zezhou himself to cover the withdrawal and summoned Liu Zhijun, military governor of Kuangguo, to march toward Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申朔，帝發大梁；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day of the month Renshen, the Emperor set out from Daliang;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day Renshen, the emperor left Daliang;

sentences.zh: 丁丑，次澤州。

translations.literal: on the day Dingchou he halted at Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: on Dingchou he reached Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，劉知俊至。

translations.literal: On the day Xinsi Liu Zhijun arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On Xinsi Liu Zhijun arrived.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以知俊為潞州行營招討使。

translations.literal: On the day Renwu he appointed Zhijun commander of the Luzhou campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On Renwu he made Zhijun commander of the Luzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，門下侍郎、同平章事張文蔚卒。

translations.literal: On the day Guisi Zhang Wenwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, died.
translations.idiomatic: On Guisi Zhang Wenwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, died.

sentences.zh: 帝以李思安久無功，亡將校四十餘人，士卒以萬計，更閉壁自守，遣使召詣行在。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Li Si'an had long achieved nothing—having lost more than forty officers and commanders and soldiers numbering in the tens of thousands—and now merely shut himself behind the walls in defense, sent an envoy summoning him to the imperial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing that Li Si'an had achieved nothing for so long—more than forty officers lost and tens of thousands of troops gone—and now only cowered behind the walls, sent for him to come to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 甲午，削思安官爵，勒歸本貫充役。

translations.literal: On the day Jiawu he stripped Si'an of rank and title and compelled him to return to his native place to serve compulsory labor.
translations.idiomatic: On Jiawu he stripped Si'an of rank and title and sent him back to his home district for corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 斬監押楊敏貞。

translations.literal: He executed the supervising officer Yang Minzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising officer Yang Minzhen was executed.

sentences.zh: 晉李嗣昭固守逾年，城中資用將竭，嗣昭登城宴諸將作樂。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao of Jin had held fast for more than a year; provisions in the city were nearly exhausted. Sizhao ascended the wall, feasted his generals, and had music played.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao of Jin had held out for more than a year; supplies in the city were almost gone. Sizhao went up on the wall, feasted his generals, and had music played.

sentences.zh: 流矢中嗣昭足，嗣昭密拔之，座中皆不覺。

translations.literal: A stray arrow struck Sizhao's foot; he secretly pulled it out, and none at the feast noticed.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow hit Sizhao in the foot; he quietly pulled it out, and no one at the feast knew.

sentences.zh: 帝數遣使賜嗣昭詔，諭降之。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly sent envoys bearing edicts to Sizhao, urging him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys again and again with edicts urging Sizhao to surrender.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭焚詔書，斬使者。

translations.literal: Sizhao burned the edicts and beheaded the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao burned the edicts and beheaded the messengers.

sentences.zh: 帝留澤州旬餘，欲召上黨兵還，遣使就與諸將議之。

translations.literal: The Emperor remained at Zezhou more than ten days and wished to recall the Shangdang army; he sent an envoy to consult with the generals on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed at Zezhou more than ten days and wanted to recall the Shangdang force; he sent someone to consult the generals on the spot.

sentences.zh: 諸將以為李克用死，余吾兵且退，上黨孤城無援，請更留旬月以俟之。

translations.literal: The generals thought that since Li Keyong was dead, the Yuyu troops would soon withdraw and Shangdang was an isolated city without support; they asked to stay another ten days or so and wait.
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued that with Li Keyong dead, the Yuyu troops would soon pull back and Shangdang was a lone city with no help coming; they asked to wait another ten days or so.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，命增運芻糧以饋其軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed and ordered more fodder and grain transported to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered more fodder and grain sent to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊將精兵萬餘人擊晉軍，斬獲甚眾，表請自留攻上黨，車駕宜還京師。

translations.literal: Liu Zhijun led more than ten thousand elite troops to strike Jin forces and killed or captured a great number. He memorialized asking to remain himself to attack Shangdang while the imperial carriage should return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhijun led more than ten thousand picked troops against the Jin army and took a heavy toll. He memorialized asking to stay and finish off Shangdang while the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以關中空虛，慮岐人侵同華，命知俊休兵長子旬日，退屯晉州，俟五月歸鎮。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Guanzhong was empty and he feared Qi people would invade Tong and Hua, ordered Zhijun to rest his troops at Changzi for ten days, fall back and encamp at Jinzhou, and return to his post in the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, with Guanzhong stripped bare and fearing a Qi thrust into Tong and Hua, ordered Zhijun to rest at Changzi ten days, fall back to Jinzhou, and return to his command in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 蜀太師王宗佶既罷相，怨望，陰畜養死士，謀作亂。

translations.literal: Wang Zongji of Shu, Grand Preceptor, having been removed from the chancellorship, nursed resentment and secretly nurtured daredevil fighters, plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongji, Grand Preceptor of Shu, removed from the chancellorship, brooded on his grievance, secretly kept a band of daredevils, and plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 上表以為：「臣官預大臣，親則長子，國家之事，休戚是同。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating: "Your servant's office ranks among the great ministers; in kinship I am the eldest son. Affairs of state—joy and sorrow are alike for me.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Your servant ranks among the great ministers and, by kinship, is the eldest son. The state's weal and woe are mine as well.

sentences.zh: 今儲貳未定，必啟厲階。

translations.literal: Now the heir apparent is not fixed—this is sure to open the door to calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is not yet named—that alone invites disaster.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以宗懿才堪繼承，宜早行冊禮，以臣為元帥，兼總六軍。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty considers Zongyi capable of succession, the investiture rites should be carried out early, with me as grand marshal concurrently commanding all six armies.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty judges Zongyi fit to succeed, invest him soon and make me grand marshal with command of all six armies.

sentences.zh: 儻以時方艱難，宗懿沖幼，臣安敢持謙不當重事！

translations.literal: If the times are truly hard and Zongyi is young and tender, how dare I hold to modesty and shun weighty affairs!
translations.idiomatic: If times are hard and Zongyi is still young, how can I cling to modesty and refuse the heavy burden!

sentences.zh: 陛下既正位南面，軍旅之事宜委之臣下。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already taken the throne facing south—the matter of armies and campaigns ought to be entrusted to your ministers below.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already faces south as sovereign—military affairs ought to be left to your ministers below.

sentences.zh: 臣請開元帥府，鑄六軍印，征戍征發，臣悉專行。

translations.literal: I ask to open a grand marshal's office, cast seals for the six armies, and have all mobilizations for campaign and garrison pass solely through me.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to open a marshal's headquarters, cast seals for the six armies, and handle every levy and deployment myself.

sentences.zh: 太子視膳於晨昏，微臣握兵於環衛，萬世基業，惟陛下裁之。」

translations.literal: The crown prince would attend to meals morning and evening; your humble servant would hold the armies in the inner guard—the foundation for ten thousand ages lies only in Your Majesty's judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Let the crown prince attend to meals morning and evening while I hold the armies at the inner guard—the foundation of ten thousand years rests with Your Majesty alone."

sentences.zh: 蜀主怒，隱忍未發，以問唐道襲，對曰：「宗佶威望，內外懾服，足以統御諸將。」

translations.literal: The Shu ruler was angry but swallowed it and did not act; he asked Tang Daoxi, who answered: "Zongji's prestige makes men within and without tremble and submit—he is enough to command all the generals."
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler was furious but held his peace and asked Tang Daoxi, who said, "Zongji's prestige awes everyone inside and out—he is fit to command the generals."

sentences.zh: 蜀主益疑之。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler grew still more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler's suspicions only deepened.

sentences.zh: 已亥，宗佶入見，辭色悖慢。

translations.literal: On the day Jihai Zongji came in audience; his words and bearing were insolent and rude.
translations.idiomatic: On Jihai Zongji came to audience; his tone and manner were brazen and rude.

sentences.zh: 蜀主諭之，宗佶不退，蜀主不堪其忿，命衛士撲殺之。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler admonished him; Zongji would not withdraw. Unable to bear his rage, the ruler ordered guards to beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler rebuked him, but Zongji would not leave. Unable to contain his anger, the ruler ordered the guards to beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 貶其黨御史中丞鄭騫為維州司戶，衛尉少卿李鋼為汶川尉，皆賜死於路。

translations.literal: His faction—the Censor-in-Chief Zheng Juan was demoted to registrar of Wei prefecture; the Vice Minister of the Guard Li Gang was made warden of Wenchuan—both were granted death on the road.
translations.idiomatic: His faction was punished: Censor-in-Chief Zheng Juan was demoted to registrar of Wei prefecture; Vice Minister of the Guard Li Gang was made warden of Wenchuan—both were ordered to die on the road.

sentences.zh: 初，晉王克用卒，周德威握重兵在外，國人皆疑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince Jin Keyong died, Zhou Dewei held heavy forces abroad and the people of the state all doubted him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince Jin Keyong died, Zhou Dewei held a large army in the field and everyone in the state was uneasy about him.

sentences.zh: 晉王存勖召德威使引兵還。

translations.literal: Prince Jin Cunxu summoned Dewei and had him lead the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Cunxu summoned Dewei and ordered him to bring the army home.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛丑朔，德威至晉陽，留兵城外，獨徒步而入，伏先王柩，哭極哀。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Xinchou, Dewei reached Jinyang, left his troops outside the walls, entered alone on foot, prostrated himself before the late king's coffin, and wept with utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Xinchou, Dewei reached Jinyang, left his troops outside the city, walked in alone, prostrated himself before the late king's coffin, and wept until he was spent.

sentences.zh: 退，謁嗣王，禮甚恭。

translations.literal: He withdrew and called on the heir prince with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and paid his respects to the new prince with the utmost courtesy.

sentences.zh: 眾心由是釋然。

translations.literal: Men's hearts were thereby set at ease.
translations.idiomatic: With that, everyone's suspicions lifted.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，門下侍郎、同平章事楊涉罷為右僕射；

translations.literal: On the day Guimao Yang She, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, was removed and made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: On Guimao Yang She, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, was dismissed and made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎于兢為中書侍郎，翰林學士承旨張策為刑部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Yu Jing was made Vice Director of the Secretariat for the Department of State Affairs; Chief Academician Zhang Ce was made Vice Minister of Justice—both as Associate Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Chief Academician Zhang Ce was made Vice Minister of Justice—both Associate Grand Councillors.

sentences.zh: 兢，琮之兄子也。

translations.literal: Jing was the nephew of Yu Cong (Yu Kan's brother's son).
translations.idiomatic: Jing was a nephew of Yu Cong.

sentences.zh: 夾寨奏余吾晉兵已引去，帝以為援兵不能復來，潞州必可取，丙午，自澤州南還；

translations.literal: The Twin Stockades reported that Jin troops at Yuyu had already withdrawn. The Emperor thought reinforcements could not come again and Luzhou was sure to be taken. On the day Bingwu he returned south from Zezhou;
translations.idiomatic: The Twin Stockades reported that the Jin force at Yuyu had withdrawn. The emperor judged that relief could not return and Luzhou was as good as his. On Bingwu he marched south from Zezhou;

sentences.zh: 壬子，至大梁。

translations.literal: on the day Renzi he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: on Renzi he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 梁兵在夾寨者亦不復設備。

translations.literal: Liang troops at the Twin Stockades likewise ceased to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang troops in the Twin Stockades likewise stopped making ready.

sentences.zh: 晉王與諸將謀曰：「上黨，河東之籓蔽，無上黨，是無河東也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin consulted his generals, saying: "Shangdang is Hedong's screen and shield. Without Shangdang there is no Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin consulted his generals: "Shangdang is Hedong's rampart. Lose Shangdang and you lose Hedong.

sentences.zh: 且朱溫所憚者獨先王耳，聞吾新立，以為童子未閒軍旅，必有驕怠之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhu Wen feared only the late king. Hearing that I have newly succeeded, he will think me a lad unversed in campaigns and is sure to grow arrogant and careless.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen feared only the late king. Hearing I have just succeeded, he will take me for a boy who knows nothing of war and grow arrogant and slack.

sentences.zh: 若簡精兵倍道趣之，出其不意，破之必矣。

translations.literal: If we pick elite troops and hurry by forced marches, striking where he does not expect it, we are certain to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Pick elite troops, march by forced stages, and strike where he does not expect it—we are sure to break them.

sentences.zh: 取威定霸，在此一舉，不可失也！」

translations.literal: To seize renown and fix hegemony lies in this one stroke—it must not be missed!"
translations.idiomatic: Glory and dominion hang on this one blow—it must not be missed!"

sentences.zh: 張承業亦勸之行。

translations.literal: Zhang Chengye also urged the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye urged the same.

sentences.zh: 乃遣承業及判官王緘乞師於鳳翔，又遣使賂契丹王阿保機求騎兵。

translations.literal: He then sent Chengye and his aide Wang Jian to beg troops from Fengxiang, and also sent envoys bribing the Khitan king Abaoji to seek cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chengye and his aide Wang Jian to beg troops from Fengxiang and also sent envoys with gifts to the Khitan king Abaoji asking for cavalry.

sentences.zh: 岐王衰老，兵弱財竭，竟不能應。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi was aged; his armies were weak and funds exhausted—ultimately he could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi was old; his troops were weak and his treasury empty—he could not help in the end.

sentences.zh: 晉王大閱士卒，以前昭義節度使丁會為都招討使。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin held a great review of troops and appointed the former military governor of Zhaoyi Ding Hui as supreme campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin held a grand review and appointed the former Zhaoyi military governor Ding Hui supreme campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帥周德威等發晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day Jiazi he led Zhou Dewei and the others out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On Jiazi he marched out of Jinyang at the head of Zhou Dewei and the rest.

sentences.zh: 淮南遣兵寇石首，襄州兵敗之於瀺港。

translations.literal: Huainan sent troops to raid Shishou; Xiang prefecture troops defeated them at Changan Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan sent troops against Shishou; Xiang forces defeated them at Changan Harbor.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將李厚將水軍萬五千趣荊南，高季昌逆戰，敗之於馬頭。

translations.literal: They also sent their general Li Hou with fifteen thousand sailors pressing toward Jingnan; Gao Jichang met them in battle and defeated them at Matou.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent the general Li Hou with fifteen thousand sailors toward Jingnan; Gao Jichang met them and defeated them at Matou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，晉王軍於黃碾，距上黨四十五里。

translations.literal: On the day Jisi the Prince of Jin encamped at Huangnian, forty-five li from Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: On Jisi the Prince of Jin camped at Huangnian, forty-five li from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛未朔，晉王伏兵三垂岡下，詰旦大霧，進兵直抵夾寨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day Xinwei, the Prince of Jin hid troops below Sanchui Ridge. At daybreak a great fog; his army advanced straight to the Twin Stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day Xinwei, the Prince of Jin hid troops below Sanchui Ridge. At dawn a heavy fog; his army went straight for the Twin Stockades.

sentences.zh: 梁軍無斥候，不意晉兵之至，將士尚未起，軍中驚擾。

translations.literal: Liang forces had no scouts; they did not expect Jin troops to arrive. Officers and men had not yet risen—the army was thrown into alarm and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang army had no scouts out and did not expect the Jin force. The men had not yet risen—the camp erupted in panic.

sentences.zh: 晉王命周德威、李嗣源分兵為二道，德威攻西北隅，嗣源攻東北隅，填塹燒寨，鼓噪而入。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin ordered Zhou Dewei and Li Siyuan to divide forces into two columns—Dewei attacked the northwest corner, Siyuan the northeast—filled moats, burned stockades, and entered with drum and shout.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin ordered Zhou Dewei and Li Siyuan to split into two wings—Dewei on the northwest, Siyuan on the northeast—filled the ditches, burned the stockades, and stormed in with drums and shouts.

sentences.zh: 梁兵大潰，南走，招討使符道昭馬倒，為晉人所殺。

translations.literal: Liang troops broke and fled south. The campaign commander Fu Daozhao's horse fell; Jin men killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang army broke and fled south. The campaign commander Fu Daozhao's horse went down and the Jin troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 失亡將校士卒以萬計，委棄資糧、器械山積。

translations.literal: Officers, commanders, and soldiers lost or killed numbered in the tens of thousands; abandoned provisions, fodder, and weapons heaped like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men lost or killed ran into the tens of thousands; abandoned grain, fodder, and arms lay in heaps like hills.

sentences.zh: 周德威等至城下，呼李嗣昭曰：「先王已薨，今王自來，破賊夾寨。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei and the others came below the wall and called to Li Sizhao: "The late king has passed; the present king has come in person and broken the enemy's Twin Stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei and the others came to the foot of the wall and called to Li Sizhao: "The late king is gone; the new king has come himself and smashed the enemy stockades.

sentences.zh: 賊已去矣，可開門！」

translations.literal: The enemy is already gone—you may open the gate!"
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is gone—open the gate!"

sentences.zh: 嗣昭不信，曰：「此必為賊所得，使來誑我耳。」

translations.literal: Sizhao did not believe it and said: "This must be someone the enemy has seized and sent to deceive me."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao did not believe it: "The enemy has caught someone and sent him to trick me."

sentences.zh: 欲射之。

translations.literal: He wished to shoot them.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to shoot them.

sentences.zh: 左右止之，嗣昭曰：「王果來，可見乎？」

translations.literal: Those beside him stopped him. Sizhao said: "If the king has truly come, may I see him?"
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him held him back. Sizhao said, "If the king has really come, may I see him?"

sentences.zh: 王自往呼之。

translations.literal: The king went himself to call out.
translations.idiomatic: The king went forward and called to him himself.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭見王白服，大慟幾絕，城中皆哭，遂開門。

translations.literal: Sizhao saw the king in white mourning dress, wept so violently he nearly died, everyone in the city wept, and they opened the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao saw the king in white mourning garb, wept until he nearly collapsed, the whole city wept with him, and the gate was opened.

sentences.zh: 初，德威與嗣昭有隙，晉王克用臨終謂晉王存勖曰：「進通忠孝，吾愛之深。

translations.literal: Earlier Dewei and Sizhao had a rift. Prince Jin Keyong on his deathbed told Prince Jin Cunxu: "Jintong is loyal and filial—I love him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dewei and Sizhao had been at odds. On his deathbed Prince Jin Keyong told Prince Jin Cunxu, "Jintong is loyal and filial—I love him dearly.

sentences.zh: 今不出重圍，豈德威不忘舊怨邪！

translations.literal: Now that he does not break out of the heavy siege, can it be that Dewei still bears the old grudge!
translations.idiomatic: He still does not break the siege—is Dewei nursing the old grudge!

sentences.zh: 汝為吾以此意諭之。

translations.literal: You must convey this meaning to him for me.
translations.idiomatic: Go and tell him what I mean.

sentences.zh: 若潞圍不解，吾死不瞑目。」

translations.literal: If the siege of Lu does not lift, I shall die with eyes unclosed."
translations.idiomatic: If the siege of Lu is not raised, I cannot close my eyes in death."

sentences.zh: 進通，嗣昭小名也。

translations.literal: Jintong was Sizhao's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Jintong" was the name Sizhao had been called as a boy.

sentences.zh: 晉王存勖以告德威，德威感泣，由是戰夾寨甚力；

translations.literal: Prince Jin Cunxu told Dewei; Dewei was moved to tears and from this fought at the Twin Stockades with great zeal;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Cunxu told Dewei; Dewei wept with emotion and from then on fought at the Twin Stockades with all his might;

sentences.zh: 既與嗣昭相見，遂歡好如初。

translations.literal: once he had met Sizhao, they were friendly again as at first.
translations.idiomatic: once he met Sizhao again, they were as close as before.

sentences.zh: 康懷貞以百餘騎自天井關遁歸。

translations.literal: Kang Huaizhen fled back with a little more than a hundred horsemen through the Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Huaizhen escaped through Tianjing Pass with just over a hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 帝聞夾寨不守，大驚，既而歎曰：「生子當如李亞子，克用為不亡矣！

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard that the Twin Stockade was lost, he was greatly alarmed; then he sighed and said, "If one is to have a son, he ought to be like Li Yaozi—then Keyong's line will not perish!
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Twin Stockade had fallen, the Emperor was stunned; then he sighed, "A man should father a son like Li Yaozi—then Li Keyong's house will never die out!

sentences.zh: 至如吾兒，豚犬耳！」

translations.literal: As for my own sons, they are piglets and curs!"
translations.idiomatic: My own boys are nothing but pigs and dogs!"

sentences.zh: 詔所在安集散兵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that scattered troops be gathered and settled wherever they were found.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every circuit to round up and settle the scattered troops.

sentences.zh: 周德威、李存璋乘勝進趣澤州，刺史王班素失人心，眾不為用。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei and Li Cunzhang pressed the victory and advanced on Ze Prefecture; the prefect Wang Ban had long lost the hearts of the people, and the masses would not obey him.
translations.idiomatic: Riding their victory, Zhou Dewei and Li Cunzhang pushed toward Zezhou; Prefect Wang Ban had already lost popular support, and his men would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 龍虎統軍牛存節自西都將兵應接夾寨潰兵，至天井關，謂其眾曰：「澤州要害地，不可失也；

translations.literal: The Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief Niu Cunjie led troops from the Western Capital to receive the routed men from the Twin Stockade; reaching the Tianjing Pass, he told his followers, "Ze Prefecture is critical ground and must not be lost;
translations.idiomatic: Niu Cunjie, supreme commander of the Dragon-Tiger Corps, marched from the western capital to gather the Twin Stockade fugitives; at Tianjing Pass he told his men, "Zezhou is vital—we cannot lose it;

sentences.zh: 雖無詔旨，當救之。」

translations.literal: though there is no imperial order, we ought to rescue it."
translations.idiomatic: even without an edict, we must save it."

sentences.zh: 眾皆不欲，曰：「晉人勝氣方銳，且眾寡不敵。」

translations.literal: The troops were all unwilling and said, "The Jin men's victorious spirit is still sharp, and moreover we are too few to match them."
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers refused: "The Jin are riding a hot streak, and we are far too few to fight them."

sentences.zh: 存節曰：「見危不救，非義也；

translations.literal: Cunjie said, "To see danger and not save others is not righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Cunjie said, "To see peril and refuse rescue is unrighteous;

sentences.zh: 畏敵強而避之，非勇也。」

translations.literal: to fear a strong foe and avoid him is not courage."
translations.idiomatic: to shrink from a strong enemy is not courage."

sentences.zh: 遂舉策引眾而前。

translations.literal: He thereupon raised his whip and led the host forward.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted his whip and drove the column ahead.

sentences.zh: 至澤州，城中人已縱火喧噪，欲應晉王，班閉牙城自守，存節至，乃定。

translations.literal: When they reached Ze Prefecture, the people inside the city had already set fires and were shouting in uproar, intending to welcome the Prince of Jin; Ban shut himself in the yamen citadel to hold out, and only when Cunjie arrived was the city settled.
translations.idiomatic: At Zezhou the townspeople were already torching buildings and clamoring to open the gates to the Jin prince; Wang Ban barricaded himself in the inner citadel until Cunjie arrived and restored order.

sentences.zh: 晉兵尋至，緣城穿地道攻之，存節晝夜拒戰，凡旬有三日。

translations.literal: Jin troops soon arrived and, running along the walls and digging underground passages, attacked; Cunjie resisted day and night for altogether thirteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces soon came up, mining and sapping along the walls; Cunjie fought them day and night for thirteen days straight.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊自晉州引兵救之，德威焚攻具，退保高平。

translations.literal: Liu Zhijun led troops from Jin Prefecture to relieve the city; Dewei burned his siege engines and withdrew to hold Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhijun marched from Jinzhou to relieve the siege; Dewei burned his siege gear and fell back to Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 晉王歸晉陽，休兵行賞。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin returned to Jinyang, rested the army, and distributed rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin prince returned to Jinyang, gave his army a rest, and handed out rewards.

sentences.zh: 以周德威為振武節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei was made military governor of Zhenwu and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei was appointed military governor of Zhenwu and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 命州縣舉賢才，黜貪殘，寬租賦，撫孤窮，伸冤濫，禁奸盜，境內大治。

translations.literal: He ordered the prefectures and counties to recommend worthy talent, dismiss the greedy and cruel, lighten land tax and corvée, comfort orphans and the destitute, redress wrongful imprisonment, and forbid banditry and theft, until the whole territory was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the districts to elevate talent, purge the corrupt, ease taxes and labor, succor widows and orphans, right judicial abuses, and suppress robbery—until his realm was thoroughly pacified.

sentences.zh: 以河東地狹兵少，乃訓練士卒，令騎兵不見敵無得乘馬。

translations.literal: Because the Hedong territory was narrow and its soldiery few, he trained the troops and ordered that cavalry must not mount unless they saw the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong was cramped and undermanned, so he drilled his troops and forbade horsemen to mount until the enemy was in sight.

sentences.zh: 部分已定，無得相逾越，及留絕以避險；

translations.literal: Once the sections were fixed, none might cross from one to another, nor linger behind to avoid danger;
translations.idiomatic: Once the companies were assigned, none could cross into another's lane or hang back to dodge danger;

sentences.zh: 分道並進，期會無得差晷刻。

translations.literal: they were to advance on separate routes in parallel and must not miss the rendezvous by so much as a quarter-hour.
translations.idiomatic: they were to advance on parallel routes and meet on the clock—not a quarter-hour late.

sentences.zh: 犯者必斬。

translations.literal: Whoever violated this was beheaded without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were beheaded without exception.

sentences.zh: 故能兼山東，取河南，由士卒精整故也。

translations.literal: Thus he could seize Shandong and take Henan—it was because his soldiers were drilled to precision.
translations.idiomatic: That was how he seized Shandong and took Henan: his men were drilled to a razor's edge.

sentences.zh: 初，晉王克用平王行瑜，唐昭宗許其承制封拜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Jin Li Keyong had pacified Wang Xingyu, Emperor Zhaozong of Tang had granted him the authority to commission and enfeoff on his own warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, after Li Keyong crushed Wang Xingyu, Emperor Zhaozong had authorized him to commission and enfeoff officers on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 時方鎮多行墨制，王恥與之同，每除吏必表聞。

translations.literal: At that time many regional commanders issued appointments in their own ink without court sanction; the Prince was ashamed to do the same and whenever he appointed an official he memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Most governors then filled posts by informal ink warrants; the prince refused to follow suit and memorialized every appointment to the court.

sentences.zh: 至是，晉王存勖始承制製除吏。

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Jin Li Cunxu at last began to exercise commissioned authority and appoint officials on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Only now did Li Cunxu begin to commission and appoint officials under his own warrant.

sentences.zh: 晉王德張承業，以兄事之，每至其第，升堂拜母，賜遺甚厚。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin honored Zhang Chengye with virtue and treated him as an elder brother; whenever he came to Zhang's residence he ascended the hall to bow to Zhang's mother, and his gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxu revered Zhang Chengye and treated him like an elder brother—each visit took him into the hall to bow to Zhang's mother, and his gifts were lavish.

sentences.zh: 潞州圍守歷年，士民凍餒死者太半，市裡蕭條。

translations.literal: The siege of Lu Prefecture had lasted a year; more than half the soldiers and civilians had died of cold and hunger, and the market streets were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Prefecture had been under siege for a year; cold and famine had killed more than half the garrison and townsfolk, and the markets stood empty.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭勸課農桑，寬租緩刑，數年之間，軍城完復。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao urged farming and sericulture, eased rents and slowed punishments; within a few years the army posts and the city were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao promoted farming and silk work, cut rents, and softened punishments; within a few years the garrison and city were whole again.

sentences.zh: 靜江節度使、同平章事李瓊卒，楚王殷以其弟永州刺史存知桂州事。

translations.literal: The Jingjiang military governor and Associate Grand Councillor Li Qiong died; the King of Chu Yin appointed his younger brother, Yong Prefecture governor Cun, to oversee Gui Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong, military governor of Jingjiang and Associate Grand Councillor, died; King Yin of Chu put his younger brother, Governor Cun of Yongzhou, in charge of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 壬申，更以許州忠武軍為匡國軍，同州匡國軍為忠武軍，陝州保義軍為鎮國軍。

translations.literal: On the day Renshen, the Zhongwu army of Xu Prefecture was renamed the Kuangguo army, the Kuangguo army of Tong Prefecture was renamed the Zhongwu army, and the Baoyi army of Shan Prefecture was renamed the Zhenguo army.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Zhongwu army at Xuzhou was renamed Kuangguo, Tongzhou's Kuangguo became Zhongwu, and Shanzhou's Baoyi became Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，楚兵寇鄂州，淮南所署知州秦裴擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day Yihai, Chu troops raided E Prefecture; Qin Pei, whom Huainan had installed as prefect, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Chu forces struck Ezhou; Qin Pei, Huainan's appointed prefect, beat them back.

sentences.zh: 淮南左牙指揮使張顥、右牙指揮使徐溫專制軍政，弘農威王心不能平，欲去之而未能。

translations.literal: The Huainan left-guard commander Zhang Hao and right-guard commander Xu Wen monopolized military and civil government; the Prince of Wei of Hongnong Yang Wo could not abide it in his heart and wished to remove them but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao of the left guard and Xu Wen of the right guard ran Huainan's army and administration; Yang Wo, Prince of Wei of Hongnong, seethed at their grip but could not shake them loose.

sentences.zh: 二人不自安，共謀弒王，分其地以臣於梁。

translations.literal: The two men felt insecure and together plotted to assassinate the Prince, divide his territory, and submit as vassals to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in their power, the two plotted to murder the prince, carve up his lands, and submit to Liang.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，顥遣其黨紀祥等弒王於寢室，詐云暴薨。

translations.literal: On the day Wuyin, Hao sent his partisans Ji Xiang and others to assassinate the Prince in his bedchamber, falsely reporting that he had died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Zhang Hao sent Ji Xiang and other henchmen to kill the prince in his chamber, then announced a sudden death.

sentences.zh: 己卯，顥集將吏於府廷，夾道及庭中堂上皆列白刃，令諸將悉去衛從然後入。

translations.literal: On the day Jimao, Hao assembled the generals and officials in the government courtyard; along the road and in the hall above and below, white blades were set in ranks, and he ordered every commander to dismiss his escort before entering.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Zhang Hao summoned the commanders to the yamen courtyard, lined the approach and hall with naked swords, and made each officer enter alone without guards.

sentences.zh: 顥厲聲問曰：「嗣王已薨，軍府誰當主之？」

translations.literal: Hao asked in a harsh voice, "The heir-prince is already dead—who should head the military government?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao demanded in a snarl, "The heir is dead—who will head this commandery?"

sentences.zh: 三問，莫應，顥氣色益怒。

translations.literal: He asked three times; no one answered, and Hao's expression grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: He asked three times; silence answered him, and his face darkened further.

sentences.zh: 幕僚嚴可求前密啟曰：「軍府至大，四境多虞，非公主之不可。

translations.literal: Staff officer Yan Keqiu stepped forward and said in a low voice, "The military government is too great and the borders too unsettled—it cannot be without a lord. Yet today would perhaps be too soon.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Yan Keqiu whispered forward, "The seat is too great and the frontiers too troubled to leave empty—but not today, surely not today.

sentences.zh: 然今日則恐太速。」

translations.literal: Hao said, "What do you mean by too soon?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao snapped, "Too soon for what?"

sentences.zh: 顥曰：「何謂速也？」

translations.literal: Keqiu said, "Liu Wei, Tao Ya, Li Yu, and Li Jian were all the late king's equals; if you seize power yourself, will these men willingly serve beneath you?
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu said, "Liu Wei, Tao Ya, Li Yu, and Li Jian stood as the late king's peers—will they bow to you if you seize the seat?

sentences.zh: 可求曰：「劉威、陶雅、李遇、李簡皆先王之等夷，公今自立，此曹肯為公下乎？

translations.literal: “Better to set up the young lord and assist him—then which commander would dare refuse!"
translations.idiomatic: “Better install the boy and guide him—who among the generals would refuse?"

sentences.zh: 不若立幼主輔之，諸將孰敢不從！」

translations.literal: Hao was silent a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao fell silent for a long while.

sentences.zh: 顥默然久之。

translations.literal: Keqiu then dismissed those at hand, quickly wrote a sheet of paper and put it in his sleeve, and waved his colleagues to go to the envoy's residence to offer congratulations; none could guess what he meant.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu sent the attendants away, scribbled a sheet into his sleeve, and waved his colleagues to the envoy's quarters to offer congratulations—none knew his design.

sentences.zh: 可求因屏左右，急書一紙置袖中，麾同列詣使宅賀，眾莫測其所為，既至，可求跪讀之，乃太夫人史氏教也。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Keqiu knelt and read it aloud—it was an instruction from the Lady Dowager Shi.
translations.idiomatic: There Keqiu knelt and read it aloud: a directive from Lady Dowager Shi.

sentences.zh: 大要言：「先王創業艱難，嗣王不幸早世，隆演次當立，諸將宜無負楊氏，善輔導之。」

translations.literal: In substance it said, "The late king founded his enterprise through hardship; the heir-prince has unfortunately died young; Longyan is next in line to be established—the generals should not fail the Yang house and should guide and support him well."
translations.idiomatic: Its gist: "Your late lord built this realm in hardship; the heir has died too young; Longyan is next in succession—do not betray the Yang clan, but guide him well."

sentences.zh: 辭旨明切。

translations.literal: The wording was clear and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: The words were plain and adamant.

sentences.zh: 顥氣色皆沮，以其義正，不敢奪，遂奉威王弟隆演稱淮南留後、東面諸道行營都統。

translations.literal: Hao's color was entirely deflated; because the argument was righteous he did not dare seize the post, and he thereupon installed the Prince of Wei's younger brother Longyan as Huainan acting governor and supreme commander of the eastern circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao's swagger collapsed; the charge was too righteous to defy, and he installed the late prince's younger brother Longyan as acting Huainan governor and supreme commander of the eastern circuits.

sentences.zh: 既罷，副都統朱瑾詣可求所居，曰：「瑾年十六七即橫戈躍馬，沖犯大敵，未嘗畏懾，今日對顥，不覺流汗，公面折之如無人。

translations.literal: When the session ended, Vice supreme commander Zhu Jin went to Keqiu's lodging and said, "From sixteen or seventeen I have brandished spear and spurred my horse, charging great enemies, and never once felt fear;
translations.idiomatic: After the assembly, deputy supreme commander Zhu Jin visited Keqiu and said, "Since I was sixteen I have taken spear and saddle against great foes and never flinched;

sentences.zh: 乃知瑾匹夫之勇，不及公遠矣。」

translations.literal: today facing Hao I broke into a sweat without noticing. You rebuked him to his face as though no one were there—I now know that my courage as a lone brawler falls far short of yours."
translations.idiomatic: yet today before Zhang Hao I sweated without knowing it. You faced him down as if he were nothing—I see now that my lone brawler's nerve is nothing beside yours."

sentences.zh: 因以兄事之。

translations.literal: He therefore treated Keqiu as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: From that day he treated Keqiu as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 顥以徐溫為浙西觀察使，鎮潤州。

translations.literal: Hao made Xu Wen observation commissioner of western Zhejiang, stationed at Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao posted Xu Wen to western Zhejiang as observation commissioner, with his seat at Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴可求說溫曰：「公捨牙兵而出外籓，顥必以弒君之罪歸公。」

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu urged Wen, "If you leave the guard troops and go out to a border fief, Hao is sure to lay the crime of regicide on you."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu warned Xu Wen, "Quit the guard for an outer post and Zhang Hao will hang regicide on you."

sentences.zh: 溫驚曰：「然則奈何？」

translations.literal: Wen said in alarm, "Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen started: "Then what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 可求曰：「顥剛愎而暗於事，公能見聽，請為公圖之。」

translations.literal: Keqiu said, "Hao is obstinate and blind to affairs; if you will heed me, let me plot for you."
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu said, "Zhang Hao is stubborn and dull—hear me out and I will lay a plan."

sentences.zh: 時副使李承嗣參預軍府之政，可求又說承嗣曰：「顥凶威如此，今出徐於外，意不徒然，恐亦非公之利。」

translations.literal: At that time Vice commissioner Li Chengsi took part in the military government's affairs; Keqiu also urged Chengsi, "Hao's ferocious power is like this; now sending Xu out on campaign is not for nothing— I fear it is not to your benefit either."
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Li Chengsi then shared in headquarters business; Keqiu told him too, "Zhang Hao's terror is plain—posting Xu Wen outside is no idle move, and it may not serve you either."

sentences.zh: 承嗣深然之。

translations.literal: Chengsi deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was thoroughly convinced.

sentences.zh: 可求往見顥曰：「右牙欲之，非吾意也。

translations.literal: Keqiu went to see Hao and said, "The right guard wanted the post—it was not my wish. The matter is already done—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu went to Zhang Hao: "The right guard wanted the assignment—not I. It is already done—what now?

sentences.zh: 業已行矣，奈何？」

translations.literal: Hao said, "It is already underway—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao said, "It has already gone forward—what then?"

sentences.zh: 可求曰：「止之易耳。」

translations.literal: Keqiu said, "Stopping it is easy."
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu said, "Stopping it is easy."

sentences.zh: 明日，可求邀顥及承嗣俱詣溫，可求瞋目責溫曰：「古人不忘一飯之恩，況公楊氏宿將！

translations.literal: The next day Keqiu invited Hao and Chengsi together to Wen's quarters; Keqiu glared and rebuked Wen, saying, "The ancients did not forget a single meal's kindness—how much more you, an old commander of the Yang house!
translations.idiomatic: Next day Keqiu brought Zhang Hao and Li Chengsi to Xu Wen's quarters, glared at Wen, and thundered, "The ancients repaid a single meal's kindness—how much more a veteran of the Yang house!

sentences.zh: 今幼嗣初立，多事之時，乃求自安於外，可乎？」

translations.literal: The young heir has just been established and this is a time of many troubles—yet you seek your own ease in the outer provinces. Is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: The boy has just taken the seat and troubles crowd on every side—will you tuck yourself away in the provinces for comfort?"

sentences.zh: 溫謝曰：「苟諸公見容，溫何敢自專！」

translations.literal: Wen apologized, saying, "If you gentlemen will tolerate me, how would Wen dare act on his own!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen bowed: "If you gentlemen will have me, how dare I go my own way!"

sentences.zh: 由是不行。

translations.literal: Because of this the transfer did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: The posting was canceled.

sentences.zh: 顥知可求陰附溫，夜，遣盜刺之，可求知不免，請為書辭府主。

translations.literal: Hao knew that Keqiu was secretly aligned with Wen; at night he sent assassins to stab him. Keqiu knew he could not escape and asked to write a farewell to the lord of the government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao knew Keqiu was in league with Xu Wen; that night he sent killers. Keqiu, seeing no escape, asked only to write a farewell to his lord.

sentences.zh: 盜執刀臨之，可求操筆無懼色。

translations.literal: The assassin held his blade over him; Keqiu took up the brush without a trace of fear.
translations.idiomatic: The blade hovered at his throat; Keqiu wrote without a tremor.

sentences.zh: 盜能辨字，見其辭旨忠壯，曰：「公長者，吾不忍殺。」

translations.literal: The assassin could read characters; seeing the wording loyal and stern, he said, "You are an elder of honor—I cannot kill you."
translations.idiomatic: The killer could read; the lines were loyal and fierce. He said, "You are a man of honor—I will not strike."

sentences.zh: 掠其財以覆命，曰：「捕之不獲。」

translations.literal: He plundered Keqiu's goods and returned to report, saying, "We pursued but could not catch him."
translations.idiomatic: He looted Keqiu's goods and reported back, "We hunted but could not take him."

sentences.zh: 顥怒曰：「吾欲得可求首，何用財為！」

translations.literal: Hao said in anger, "I wanted Keqiu's head—what use is wealth!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao raged, "I wanted Keqiu's head—what good is loot!"

sentences.zh: 溫與可求謀誅顥，可求曰：「非鍾泰章不可。」

translations.literal: Wen and Keqiu plotted to kill Hao; Keqiu said, "Without Zhong Taizhang it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen and Keqiu plotted Zhang Hao's death; Keqiu said, "Only Zhong Taizhang can do it."

sentences.zh: 泰章者，合肥人，時為左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: Taizhang was a man of Hefei and at the time was Left Gate Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhang, a native of Hefei, then served as general of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 溫使親將彭城翟虔告之。

translations.literal: Wen sent his intimate commander Zhai Qian of Pengcheng to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen sent his trusted Pengcheng officer Zhai Qian to tell him.

sentences.zh: 泰章聞之喜，密結壯士三十人，夜，刺血相飲為誓。

translations.literal: When Taizhang heard it he rejoiced; in secret he gathered thirty stout fellows, and at night they pricked their arms and drank blood together in oath.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhang rejoiced at the word, secretly rallied thirty stout men, and at night they pricked their arms and swore over blood.

sentences.zh: 丁亥旦，直入斬顥於牙堂，並其親近。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day Dinghai they went straight in and beheaded Hao in the guard hall, together with his intimates.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on dinghai they burst into the guard hall and cut down Zhang Hao and his intimates.

sentences.zh: 溫始暴顥弒君之罪，轘紀祥等於市。

translations.literal: Wen then publicly exposed Hao's crime of regicide and dismembered Ji Xiang and the others in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen then proclaimed Zhang Hao's regicide and dismembered Ji Xiang and the rest in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 詣西宮白太夫人。

translations.literal: He went to the western palace to report to the Lady Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the western palace to inform the Lady Dowager.

sentences.zh: 太夫人恐懼，大泣曰：「吾兒沖幼，禍難如此，願保百口歸廬州，公之惠也。」

translations.literal: The Lady Dowager was afraid and wept greatly, saying, "My son is still young and calamity has come to such a pass; I beg only that you spare our hundred mouths and let us return to Luzhou—your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the Lady Dowager wept, "My son is still a child and disaster has struck so hard—spare our household of a hundred souls and let us return to Luzhou; that will be your mercy."

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「張顥弒逆，不可不誅，夫人宜自安。」

translations.literal: Wen said, "Zhang Hao committed treason and regicide and could not go unpunished; the Lady Dowager should set her mind at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen said, "Zhang Hao's treason could not go unpunished; Lady Dowager, be at peace."

sentences.zh: 初，顥與溫謀弒威王，溫曰：「參用左、右牙兵，心必不一，不若獨用吾兵。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao and Wen had plotted to assassinate the Prince of Wei, Wen said, "If we use both left and right guard troops together, their hearts will surely not be one—it is better to use only my troops alone."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hao and Xu Wen had first plotted against the Prince of Wei, Xu Wen had said, "Use both guards together and their hearts will split—better use only my men."

sentences.zh: 顥不可，溫曰：「然則獨用公兵。」

translations.literal: Hao would not agree; Wen said, "Then use only your troops alone."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao refused; Xu Wen said, "Then use only yours."

sentences.zh: 顥從之。

translations.literal: Hao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao agreed.

sentences.zh: 至是，窮治逆黨，皆左牙兵，也由是人以溫為實不知謀也。

translations.literal: Now, in pursuing the rebels to the end, all were left-guard soldiers; hence people took Wen to have truly not known of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Now the purge fell entirely on left-guard men, and people concluded Xu Wen had never shared the plot.

sentences.zh: 隆演以溫為左、右牙都指揮使，軍府事咸取決焉。

translations.literal: Longyan made Wen commander of both left and right guard armies, and all military-government affairs were decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: Longyan made Xu Wen commander of both guards, and every matter of the headquarters passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 以嚴可求為揚州司馬。

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu was made Yangzhou marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu was appointed marshal of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 溫性沉毅，自奉簡儉，雖不知書，使人讀獄訟之辭而決之，皆中情理。

translations.literal: Wen's nature was deep and resolute; he maintained himself in plain frugality; though he did not know writing, he had others read the words of prison litigation and decided them, and all hit the middle of reason.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen was grave and sparing; though illiterate, he had petitions and suits read aloud and judged them squarely every time.

sentences.zh: 先是，張顥用事，刑戮酷濫，給親兵剽奪市里。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Hao held power, punishments and executions were cruel and excessive, and he supplied his personal troops by plundering the market wards.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Hao's rule punishments had been savage and his personal guard had looted the markets.

sentences.zh: 溫謂嚴可求曰：「大事已定，吾與公輩當力行善政，使人解衣而寢耳。」

translations.literal: Wen said to Yan Keqiu, "The great affair is settled—we and our peers ought to exert ourselves in good government, so that people may unbind their coats and sleep in peace."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen told Yan Keqiu, "The crisis is past—you and I must govern well until people can sleep with their coats off."

sentences.zh: 乃立法度，禁強暴，舉大綱，軍民安之。

translations.literal: He thereupon established laws and regulations, forbade violence, and set out the great principles, and soldiers and civilians were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He framed laws, curbed violence, and laid down the broad rules until soldiers and civilians rested easy.

sentences.zh: 溫以軍旅委可求，以財賦委支計官駱知祥，皆稱其職，淮南謂之「嚴、駱」。

translations.literal: Wen entrusted military affairs to Keqiu and finances to the revenue officer Luo Zhixiang; both were praised for fulfilling their duties, and Huainan called them "Yan and Luo."
translations.idiomatic: He gave the army to Keqiu and the ledgers to Luo Zhixiang; both excelled, and Huainan spoke of "Yan and Luo."

sentences.zh: 己丑，契丹王阿保機遣使隨高頎入貢，且求冊命。

translations.literal: On the day Jichou, the Khitan king Abaoji sent envoys accompanying Gao Yan to present tribute and also to request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Khitan ruler Abaoji sent envoys with Gao Yan to pay tribute and seek investiture.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣司農卿渾特賜以手詔，約共滅沙陀，乃行封冊。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Court of Imperial Granaries director Hun Te with an imperial letter in hand, agreeing to destroy the Shatuo together, and only then would he proceed with enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Hun Te of the Court of Imperial Granaries with a handwritten edict: ally to crush the Shatuo, and enfeoffment would follow.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，夾寨諸將詣闕待罪，皆赦之。

translations.literal: On the day Renchen, the generals of the Twin Stockade came to the court to await punishment; all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Twin Stockade commanders presented themselves at court to await punishment; the Emperor pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 帝賞牛存節全澤州之功，以為六軍馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: The Emperor rewarded Niu Cunjie for preserving Ze Prefecture and made him commander of horse and foot of the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rewarded Niu Cunjie for saving Zezhou and made him commander of the Six Armies' horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 雷彥恭引沅江環朗州以自守，秦彥暉頓兵月餘不戰，彥恭守備稍懈。

translations.literal: Lei Yangong led the Yuan River around Lang Prefecture to hold himself secure; Qin Yanhui camped his army for more than a month without fighting, and Yangong's defenses gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yangong ringed Langzhou with the Yuan River for defense; Qin Yanhui sat before the walls for a month without battle, and Yangong's guard grew slack.

sentences.zh: 彥暉使裨將曹德昌帥壯士夜入自水竇，內外舉火相應，城中驚亂，彥暉鼓譟壞門而入，彥恭輕舟奔廣陵。
